title.zh: 卷305 列傳九十二 钱陈群 钱汝诚 钱臻 沈德潜 金德瑛 钱载 齐召南 陈兆仑 孙桂生 董邦达 钱维城 邹一桂 谢墉 金甡 庄存与 刘星炜 王昶
title.en: Volume 305 Biographies 92: Qian Chenqun, Qian Rucheng, Qian Zhen, Shen Deqian, Jin Deying, Qian Zai, Qi Zhaonan, Chen Zhaolun, Sun Guisheng, Dong Bangda, Qian Weicheng, Zou Yigui, Xie Yong, Jin Shen, Zhuang Cunyu, Liu Xingwei, Wang Chang
title.raw: 卷305 列傳九十二 钱陈群 钱汝诚 钱臻 沈德潜 金德瑛 钱载 齐召南 陈兆仑 孙桂生 董邦达 钱维城 邹一桂 谢墉 金甡 庄存与 刘星炜 王昶

sentences.zh: 錢陳群，字主敬，浙江嘉興人。

translations.literal: Qian Chenqun, style name Zhujing, was a native of Jiaxing, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chenqun, whose style name was Zhujing, came from Jiaxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父綸光，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Lun'guang died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Lun'guang, died while Chenqun was still young.

sentences.zh: 母陳，翼諸孤以長，語在列女傳。

translations.literal: His mother, née Chen, supported the orphans and raised them; her story is in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Chen, sheltered the orphans and brought them up; her life is recorded in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十四年，聖祖南巡，陳群迎駕吳江，獻詩。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Kangxi, when the Sacred Ancestor made a southern tour, Chenqun met the imperial procession at Wujiang and presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of the Kangxi reign, when the Kangxi Emperor toured the south, Chenqun welcomed the imperial entourage at Wujiang and offered a poem.

sentences.zh: 上命俟回蹕召試，以母陳病不赴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that he await the return of the imperial carriage for a summoned examination; because his mother Chen was ill, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to wait until the tour ended and then present himself for an examination, but he declined because his mother Chen was ill.

sentences.zh: 六十年，成進士，引見，上諭及前事。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he passed the metropolitan examination, was presented to the throne, and the emperor mentioned the earlier matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he became a jinshi, was granted an audience, and the emperor alluded to what had happened before.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，世宗命從史貽直、杭奕祿赴陝西宣諭化導，陳群週曆諸府縣，集諸生就公廨講經，反覆深切，有聞而流涕者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor ordered him to follow Shi Yizhi and Hang Yilu to Shaanxi to proclaim edicts and guide reform; Chenqun toured the prefectures and counties, gathered students at the government offices to lecture on the classics, and spoke with such repeated depth that some who heard him wept.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor sent him with Shi Yizhi and Hang Yilu to Shaanxi to proclaim imperial policy and promote moral instruction. Chenqun traveled through the prefectures and counties, assembled students in the yamen to expound the classics, and spoke with such earnest repetition that some listeners were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 使還，上諭獎為「安分讀書人」。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, the emperor praised him in an edict as "a man of books who knows his place."
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission, the emperor commended him in an edict as "a dutiful scholar."

sentences.zh: 五遷右通政，督順天學政。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Right Commissioner of Communications and supervised education in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted five times, he rose to Right Commissioner of Communications and served as educational commissioner for Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以母喪去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he resigned his post to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，高宗命仍督順天學政，除原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the Gaozong Emperor ordered him to continue supervising Shuntian education and restored his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, the Qianlong Emperor reappointed him educational commissioner for Shuntian and restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 陳群以母陳夜紡授經圖奏上，上為題詞。

translations.literal: Chenqun memorialized with a painting of his mother Chen spinning by night while teaching the classics, and the emperor inscribed a poem on it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqun presented a painting of Lady Chen spinning at night while instructing him in the classics, and the emperor composed an inscription for it.

sentences.zh: 疏請增順天鄉試中額，上以官制有定，取者多，用者益遠，國家不能收科目取人之效，寢其議。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested an increase in the provincial examination quota for Shuntian; the emperor held that official regulations were fixed, that the more men were selected the farther they were from employment, and that the state could not reap the benefit of recruitment through the examination system, and shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to enlarge the quota for provincial graduates in Shuntian, but the emperor replied that official establishments were fixed: the more candidates were passed, the fewer could actually be employed, so the state would not gain from expanding the examination intake, and the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 三遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became a Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became a Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳群屢有建白：嘗疏請嚴治匿名揭帖，無論事鉅細，非據實首告而編造歌謠詩詞，匿名粘貼閭巷街衢，當下刑部依律治罪。

translations.literal: Chenqun repeatedly offered proposals: he once memorialized requesting strict punishment of anonymous placards; regardless of whether the matter was great or small, if one fabricated songs, ballads, or verses and posted them anonymously in lanes and streets without lodging a truthful first report, the Ministry of Punishments should at once punish according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqun made many policy recommendations. He once urged severe penalties for anonymous placards: whether the matter was grave or trivial, anyone who invented songs or verses and posted them anonymously in the streets instead of making a truthful report should be prosecuted immediately by the Ministry of Punishments under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 疏請廣勸種植樹木，官地令官種，州郡吏種至千本以上，予紀錄；

translations.literal: He memorialized urging broad encouragement of planting trees: on official land officials were to plant; prefectural and district clerks who planted a thousand or more were to receive a record of merit;
translations.idiomatic: He urged wider encouragement of tree planting: on government land officials should plant trees themselves, and prefectural and district officers who planted a thousand or more were to receive a merit notation;

sentences.zh: 受代時具冊，備地方公用。

translations.literal: on leaving office they were to prepare registers for local public use.
translations.idiomatic: on completing their term they were to compile registers for local public use.

sentences.zh: 民地令民種，至五六百本者，予扁額獎賞，成材後聽取用。

translations.literal: On private land the people were to plant; those who reached five or six hundred trees were to receive inscribed plaques and rewards, and after the trees matured they might take them for use.
translations.idiomatic: On private land commoners were to plant; those who raised five or six hundred trees were to be rewarded with inscribed plaques, and once the timber matured they might use it as they wished.

sentences.zh: 疏請偏災蠲免分數，分別貧富，富者按例定分數蠲免，貧者被災幾分即蠲免幾分，使之相等。

translations.literal: He memorialized that in partial disasters the proportion of tax remission should distinguish rich and poor: the rich should receive remission by the statutory proportion, while the poor should be remitted in proportion to the degree of disaster they suffered, so that the effect would be equal.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that when only part of a region suffered disaster, remissions should distinguish rich from poor: the wealthy would receive the statutory proportional relief, while the poor would be exempted in full proportion to their losses, so that relief would be equitable.

sentences.zh: 及敕詢州縣耗羨，疏言：「康熙間，州縣官額徵錢糧，收耗羨一二錢不等。

translations.literal: When an edict inquired about surcharges collected by prefectures and counties, he memorialized: "In the Kangxi period, prefectural and county officials collected grain taxes at the assessed quota and took surcharges of one or two cash, not all alike.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered an inquiry into local surcharges on tax collection, he wrote: "Under Kangxi, prefectural and county officials collected the assessed grain taxes and took surcharges of one or two cash, varying by place.

sentences.zh: 陸隴其知嘉定縣止收四分，清如隴其，亦未聞全去耗羨也。

translations.literal: Lu Longqi as magistrate of Jiading took only four parts in ten; even officials as pure as Longqi were not heard to abolish surcharges entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Longqi as magistrate of Jiading took only four-tenths; even men as incorruptible as Longqi were never known to abolish surcharges altogether.

sentences.zh: 議者以康熙間無耗羨，非無耗羨也，特無耗羨之名耳。

translations.literal: Those who argued that there were no surcharges in the Kangxi period were mistaken: it was not that there were none, only that they had no name as surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: Those who claimed the Kangxi era had no surcharges were wrong: the surcharges existed; they simply lacked that label.

sentences.zh: 世宗出自獨斷，通計外吏大小員數，酌定養廉，而以所入耗羨按季支領。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor acted from his own judgment, calculated the number of local officials great and small, fixed integrity-nurturing stipends, and had the surcharge revenue disbursed by quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor decided on his own authority, reckoned the number of local officials at every level, set integrity-nurturing stipends, and arranged for surcharge income to be paid out quarterly.

sentences.zh: 吏治肅清，民亦安業。

translations.literal: Official discipline was purified and the people also settled in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Government was cleansed and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 特以有徵報支收之令，不知者或以為加賦。

translations.literal: Only because there was an order to report collections and disburse payments, the uninformed sometimes took it for an added levy.
translations.idiomatic: Because collections and disbursements were now formally reported, the uninformed sometimes mistook the system for a new tax.

sentences.zh: 皇上詢及盈廷，臣請稍為變通，凡耗羨所入，仍歸籓庫，各官養廉及各州縣公項，如舊支給。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty inquired and the whole court was filled with discussion, your servant requests a slight adjustment: all surcharge receipts should again go to the provincial treasury, and officials' integrity stipends and each prefecture and county's public expenses should be paid as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty raised the question and the whole court debated it, I beg a modest adjustment: all surcharge receipts should return to the provincial treasury, while officials' integrity stipends and each locality's public expenses should be paid as before.

sentences.zh: 其續增公用，名色不能畫一，多寡亦有不同，應令直省督撫明察，某件應動正項，某件應入公用，分別報銷。

translations.literal: As for newly added public expenses, the categories cannot be uniform and the amounts also differ; governors-general and governors of each province should be ordered to examine clearly which items should draw on regular revenue and which should enter public funds, and report reimbursement separately.
translations.idiomatic: For newly added public expenses, categories cannot be standardized and amounts vary; each governor-general and governor should determine which items must come from regular revenue and which from public funds, and report them separately for reimbursement.

sentences.zh: 各省州縣自酌定養廉，榮悴不一，其有支絀者，應令督撫確察量增，俾稍寬裕。

translations.literal: In each province the prefectures and counties fixed their own integrity stipends, and prosperity and hardship were not alike; where there was shortfall, governors should be ordered to investigate accurately and increase as needed so that officials would be somewhat more comfortable.
translations.idiomatic: Because each locality set its own integrity stipends, some officials remained short while others were comfortable; where stipends fell short, governors should investigate and increase them so that officials could live with modest ease.

sentences.zh: 仍飭勿得耗外加耗，以致累民。

translations.literal: They should still be instructed not to add surcharges upon surcharges and thereby burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: They must still be forbidden to pile surcharge upon surcharge and burden the people.

sentences.zh: 則既無加賦之名，並無全用耗羨辦公之事，州縣各有贏餘，益知鼓勵。

translations.literal: Then there would be neither the name of an added levy nor the practice of conducting all public business wholly from surcharges; prefectures and counties would each have surpluses and be all the more encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Then there would be no appearance of a new tax, nor the impression that all official business was paid from surcharges alone; counties would retain surpluses and officials would be better motivated.

sentences.zh: 至於施從其厚，斂從其薄，古之制也。

translations.literal: As for giving generously and collecting lightly, that was the ancient rule.
translations.idiomatic: To give generously and collect lightly was the ancient principle.

sentences.zh: 及此倉庾充裕、民安物阜之時，大臣悉心調劑，使養廉之入，不為素餐，元氣培扶，帑藏盈溢，然後以三十年之通制國用。

translations.literal: At this time when granaries are full and the people are secure and goods abundant, great ministers should carefully balance affairs so that integrity stipends are not payment for idleness, vital energy is nurtured, the treasury overflows, and only then regulate national expenditure on a thirty-year average.
translations.idiomatic: Now that granaries are full and the realm enjoys peace and plenty, senior ministers should carefully adjust affairs so that integrity stipends reward real service, the state's vital strength is sustained, and the treasury grows abundant—only then should national expenditure be planned on a thirty-year average.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖能罷羨餘，臣固知皇上之聖，不必廷臣建白如張全操其人者，而德音自下也。」

translations.literal: Song Taizu was able to abolish surplus tribute; your servant firmly knows Your Majesty's sagacity and need not wait for a court minister like Zhang Quancao to propose it, for beneficent words will issue from below."
translations.idiomatic: Song Taizu was able to abolish surplus levies; I know well that Your Majesty's wisdom needs no courtier like Zhang Quancao to propose reforms—Your gracious policy will issue of itself."

sentences.zh: 七年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上令廷臣議州縣常平倉應行諸事，諸臣皆議歉歲減價。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered court ministers to discuss what the prefectural and county ever-normal granaries should do; the ministers all proposed reducing prices in years of scarcity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court to discuss operations of the local ever-normal granaries; the ministers all favored lowering prices in famine years.

sentences.zh: 陳群疏言：「成熟之年，出陳易新，倉米必不及市米，而民以米值納倉，銀色當高於市易。

translations.literal: Chenqun memorialized: "In years of abundance, when old grain is released and new grain stored, granary rice must fall short of market rice, yet the people pay grain into the granary at rice value, so the silver rate should be higher than market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqun argued: "In good harvest years, when old grain is sold off and new grain stored, granary rice is inferior to market grain, yet commoners pay in grain at its cash value, so the rate in silver should be higher than the market price.

sentences.zh: 擬令石減一錢二分，還倉時加穀四五升，以為出入耗費。」

translations.literal: It is proposed to reduce one cash and two fen per picul, and when grain is returned to the granary to add four or five sheng per picul as allowance for loss in handling."
translations.idiomatic: I propose reducing the price by one cash and two fen per picul, and when grain is returned to the granary adding four or five sheng per picul to cover handling loss."

sentences.zh: 十七年，患反穀疾，連疏乞解職，許之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he suffered from regurgitation of grain and repeatedly memorialized requesting release from office; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he fell ill with a digestive disorder and repeatedly asked to resign; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 命其子編修汝誠侍行，且賜詩以寬其意。

translations.literal: His son the compiler Rucheng was ordered to attend him on the journey, and a poem was bestowed to comfort his mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his son, the compiler Rucheng, to accompany him home and granted a poem to console him.

sentences.zh: 陳群進途中所作詩，上為答和。

translations.literal: Chenqun presented poems composed on the road, and the emperor replied in matching verse.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqun presented poems written on the journey, and the emperor answered them in verse.

sentences.zh: 時有偽為孫嘉淦疏稿語謗上，上令窮治，陳群自家密疏請省株連，上嚴飭之，而事漸解。

translations.literal: At the time someone forged a memorial draft in Sun Jiagan's name slandering the emperor; the emperor ordered a thorough investigation. Chenqun from home sent a secret memorial asking to limit implicated kin; the emperor sternly rebuked him, yet the affair gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a forged memorial attributed to Sun Jiagan slandered the throne, and the emperor ordered a full investigation. Chenqun privately memorialized from home asking that punishment not extend to innocent families; the emperor rebuked him sharply, but the case gradually died down.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，令在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor toured the south, he was ordered to draw salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, during the southern tour, he was allowed to draw his salary while living in retirement at home.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上為橋梓圖寄賜陳群。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor had a painting of father and son sent as a gift to Chenqun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor sent Chenqun a painting of father and son as a gift.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕江南在籍侍郎沈德潛詣京師祝皇太后七十壽，命與香山九老會，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with the retired Jiangnan vice minister Shen Deqian, he went to the capital to congratulate the Empress Dowager on her seventieth birthday; he was ordered to join the Nine Elders of Fragrant Hills and was given the titular rank of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he traveled to the capital with the retired Jiangnan vice minister Shen Deqian to celebrate the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday, was invited to join the Nine Elders of Fragrant Hills, and received the titular rank of Minister.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「明歲南巡，諸臣今年已赴闕，毋更遠迎。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Next year on the southern tour, since you ministers have already come to court this year, do not again go far to meet the procession."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "On next year's southern tour, you have already come to court this year, so do not travel far again to welcome the imperial procession."

sentences.zh: 二十七年，南巡，陳群偕德潛迎駕常州，上賜詩稱為「大老」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, on the southern tour, Chenqun with Deqian met the imperial procession at Changzhou; the emperor bestowed a poem calling him "great elder."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, during the southern tour, Chenqun and Deqian welcomed the emperor at Changzhou, and the emperor granted a poem addressing him as "venerable elder."

sentences.zh: 三十年，南巡，复迎駕。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, on the southern tour, he again met the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, on another southern tour, he again welcomed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是歲陳群年八十，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: That year Chenqun was eighty and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chenqun turned eighty and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賜其子汝器舉人，汝誠扈蹕，命從還省視。

translations.literal: His son Ruqi was granted the rank of provincial graduate; Rucheng attended the imperial retinue and was ordered to return with him to visit home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruqi was granted the rank of provincial graduate; Rucheng, who was attending the emperor, was ordered to return home with his father for a visit.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，陳群復進其母陳畫冊，冊有綸光題句。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Chenqun again presented an album of paintings of his mother Chen; the album bore inscriptions by Lun'guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Chenqun again presented an album of paintings of Lady Chen, with inscriptions by his father Lun'guang.

sentences.zh: 上題詩以趙孟頫、管道升為比。

translations.literal: The emperor inscribed a poem comparing them to Zhao Mengfu and Guan Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a poem on it comparing mother and son to Zhao Mengfu and Guan Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上六十萬壽，命德潛至嘉興勸陳群毋詣京師，陳群獻竹根如意，上批劄云：「未頒僧紹之賜，恰致公遠之貢，文而有節，把玩良怡！

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, on the emperor's sixtieth birthday, Deqian was ordered to Jiaxing to urge Chenqun not to go to the capital; Chenqun presented a root-carved ruyi scepter of bamboo, and the emperor wrote on the reply: "Before the gift of Seng Shao has been bestowed, you have fittingly offered Gong Yuan's tribute—elegant yet principled, a delight to handle!
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, for the emperor's sixtieth birthday, Shen Deqian was sent to Jiaxing to persuade Chenqun not to travel to the capital; Chenqun presented a bamboo-root ruyi scepter, and the emperor wrote in reply: "Before I have granted Seng Shao's gift, you have aptly offered Gong Yuan's tribute—refined yet steadfast, a pleasure to hold!

sentences.zh: 今賜卿木蘭所獲鹿，服食延年，以俟清晤。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you the deer obtained at Mulan, to eat and prolong life, until we meet in clear converse."
translations.idiomatic: I now send you the deer taken at the Mulan hunt—eat it for long life until we meet again in person."

sentences.zh: 三十六年，上東巡，陳群迎駕平原，進登岱祝釐頌。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the emperor toured the east; Chenqun met the procession at Pingyuan and presented a prayer and hymn for ascending Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year, on the eastern tour, Chenqun welcomed the emperor at Pingyuan and presented a prayer and hymn for the Mount Tai rites.

sentences.zh: 是冬，复詣京師祝皇太后八十萬壽，命紫禁城騎馬，賜人葠，再與香山九老會。

translations.literal: That winter he again went to the capital to celebrate the Empress Dowager's eightieth birthday, was permitted to ride a horse in the Forbidden City, was given ginseng, and again joined the Nine Elders of Fragrant Hills.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned to the capital for the Empress Dowager's eightieth birthday, was allowed to ride a horse within the Forbidden City, received a gift of ginseng, and again joined the Nine Elders of Fragrant Hills.

sentences.zh: 陳群進和詩有句云「鹿馴岩畔當童扶」，上賞其超逸，復為圖賜之。

translations.literal: In a responsive poem Chenqun had a line saying "the deer is tame beside the cliff as a boy should support it"; the emperor admired its transcendent spirit and again made a painting to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: In a responsive poem Chenqun wrote, "The deer is tame beside the cliff, as a boy might steady it"; the emperor admired its free spirit and sent him another painting as a gift.

sentences.zh: 南歸，以詩餞。

translations.literal: On his return south, the emperor saw him off with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned south, the emperor bade him farewell in verse.

sentences.zh: 陳群里居，每歲上錄寄詩百餘篇，陳群必賡和，親書冊以進，體兼行草，屢蒙獎許。

translations.literal: While Chenqun lived at home, each year the emperor sent him a recorded collection of more than a hundred poems; Chenqun always responded in matching verse, personally wrote them in albums and presented them, in styles mixing regular and cursive script, and was repeatedly praised.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement Chenqun received each year more than a hundred poems the emperor had recorded and sent to him; Chenqun always wrote matching poems, copied them by hand in albums for presentation, in a style blending regular and cursive script, and was repeatedly commended.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「儒臣老輩中能以詩文結恩遇、備商榷者，沈德潛卒後惟陳群。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Among the elder generation of Confucian ministers who could form an imperial bond through poetry and prose and serve for consultation, after Shen Deqian's death only Chenqun remained."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Among the older Confucian ministers who won the throne's favor through poetry and prose and were consulted on policy, after Shen Deqian's death only Chenqun remained."

sentences.zh: 加太傅，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上製懷舊詩，列五詞臣中。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year the emperor composed a poem recalling old companions and listed him among five literary ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year the emperor wrote a nostalgic poem and named him among five literary ministers.

sentences.zh: 子汝誠，字立之。

translations.literal: His son Rucheng, style name Lizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rucheng, whose style name was Lizhi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年進士，改庶吉士，授編修，命南書房行走。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Qianlong, he became a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed compiler, and was ordered to serve in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, was appointed compiler, and was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 四遷至侍郎，歷兵、刑、戶諸部。

translations.literal: After four promotions he reached vice minister and served in the Boards of War, Punishments, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted four times, he rose to vice minister and served in the Boards of War, Punishments, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 再典試江南，上命寄諭尹繼善，招陳群遊攝山，父子可相見。

translations.literal: When he again served as chief examiner for Jiangnan, the emperor ordered a message sent to Yin Jishan to invite Chenqun to visit Mount She, so father and son might meet.
translations.idiomatic: When he again served as chief examiner for Jiangnan, the emperor instructed Yin Jishan to invite Chenqun to Mount She so father and son could meet.

sentences.zh: 汝誠試畢，迎陳群入試院，居數日乃還。

translations.literal: When Rucheng finished the examination, he welcomed Chenqun into the examination compound; after several days he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the examinations ended, Rucheng brought Chenqun into the examination compound, where he stayed several days before returning home.

sentences.zh: 三十年，乞養歸。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he requested leave to nurse his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he asked to retire and care for his parents at home.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，父喪終，授刑部侍郎，仍在南書房行走。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when mourning for his father ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and still served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, after his father's mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and continued to serve in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 汝誠子臻，字潤齋。

translations.literal: Rucheng's son Zhen, style name Runzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Rucheng's son Zhen, whose style name was Runzhai.

sentences.zh: 自兵馬司副指揮授河南鄧州知州，累遷江西糧道。

translations.literal: From deputy commander of the Horse and Chariot Office he was appointed magistrate of Dengzhou in Henan, and was promoted repeatedly to grain intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as deputy commander of the Horse and Chariot Office, he was appointed magistrate of Dengzhou in Henan and rose through successive posts to grain intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 左授山西平陽知府，复累遷直隸布政使。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi, then again promoted repeatedly to provincial treasurer of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi, he was later promoted again through successive posts to provincial treasurer of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十一年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江西南昌諸府食淮鹽，而與福建、浙江、廣東三省毗連，私販侵引額。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi the prefectures around Nanchang consumed Huai salt, yet bordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong, and smugglers encroached on the quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi the Nanchang region consumed Huai salt, but because the province bordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong, smugglers encroached on the official quota.

sentences.zh: 臻議疏綱額、緝私販。

translations.literal: Zhen proposed loosening the quota and suppressing smugglers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen proposed easing the quota and cracking down on smuggling.

sentences.zh: 尋移山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 兗、曹、沂諸府民素悍，染邪教，盜甚熾。

translations.literal: The people of the prefectures Yan, Cao, and Yi had long been fierce, were infected with heterodox sects, and banditry was very rampant.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yan, Cao, and Yi prefectures had long been unruly, were drawn to heterodox sects, and banditry flourished.

sentences.zh: 臻請就諸府增設參將以下官，上皆採其議。

translations.literal: Zhen requested that in these prefectures posts be added down to regional commander; the emperor adopted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked that additional military officers down to the rank of regional commander be stationed in those prefectures, and the emperor approved all his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 入覲，以衰老左授湖南布​​政使，休致。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court, because of age he was demoted to provincial treasurer of Hunan and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented himself at court, he was demoted because of age to provincial treasurer of Hunan and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 道光十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang he died.

sentences.zh: 陳群詩純愨樸厚，如其為人。

translations.literal: Chenqun's poetry was pure, sincere, plain, and substantial, like the man himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chenqun's poetry was plain, sincere, and unadorned, like the man himself.

sentences.zh: 賡唱既久，亦頗斅御製詩體。

translations.literal: After exchanging responsive verse for so long, he also came rather to mold himself to the style of the emperor's composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: After years of poetic exchange with the emperor, he also came to echo the style of imperial verse.

sentences.zh: 貳刑部十年，慎於庶獄，虛衷詳鞫。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of punishments for ten years, was cautious in ordinary cases, and examined with open mind and thorough inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He served ten years as vice minister of punishments, handled ordinary cases with care, and investigated each with an open mind and thorough inquiry.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗以於定國期之。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor once expected of him what was expected of Yu Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor once compared him to the Han minister Yu Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 汝誠繼貳刑部，奉陳群之教，持法明允。

translations.literal: Rucheng later served as vice minister of punishments, followed Chenqun's teaching, and upheld the law with clarity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Rucheng later served as vice minister of punishments, followed his father's teaching, and applied the law with clarity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 臻亦善治獄。

translations.literal: Zhen was also skilled in handling cases.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was also skilled at judging cases.

sentences.zh: 在平陽，介休民被盜殺其母，攫釧去。

translations.literal: At Pingyang, a man of Jiexiu was robbed and his mother killed; her bracelet was snatched away.
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Pingyang, a man from Jiexiu was robbed; his mother was killed and her bracelet taken.

sentences.zh: 民言姻家嘗貸釧，傭或竊釧逃，鄰家子左右之。

translations.literal: The man said his wife's family had once lent the bracelet, that a hired man might have stolen it and fled, and that a neighbor's son had helped him.
translations.idiomatic: The man claimed his in-laws had once lent the bracelet, that a hired servant might have stolen it and fled, and that a neighbor's son had assisted him.

sentences.zh: 縣捕三人，榜掠誣服。

translations.literal: The county arrested three men; under beating they falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate arrested three men, who under torture falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 他日獲盜得釧，民乃言非其母物。

translations.literal: Another day the thief was caught and the bracelet recovered; the man then said it was not his mother's property.
translations.idiomatic: Later the real thief was caught with the bracelet, and the man admitted it had not belonged to his mother.

sentences.zh: 獄不能決。

translations.literal: The case could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: The case could not be resolved.

sentences.zh: 臻微服訪得實。

translations.literal: Zhen in plain dress investigated and obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen went in disguise and uncovered the truth.

sentences.zh: 撫山東，清庶獄，雪非罪二十餘人，擒教訟者置於法。

translations.literal: As governor of Shandong he cleared ordinary cases, exonerated more than twenty wrongly convicted men, and seized those who taught litigation and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Shandong he cleared ordinary cases, exonerated more than twenty innocent men, and arrested professional litigators and punished them under the law.

sentences.zh: 沈德潛，字碻士，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Shen Deqian, style name Qieshi, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Deqian, whose style name was Qieshi, came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉博學鴻詞，試未入選。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the Erudite Letters examination and was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the special Erudite Letters examination but was not selected.

sentences.zh: 四年，成進士，改庶吉士，年六十七矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he passed the metropolitan examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was already sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became a jinshi and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 七年，散館，日晡，高宗蒞視，問孰為德潛者，稱以「江南老名士」，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, upon completion of Hanlin probation, in the late afternoon the Qianlong Emperor came to inspect and asked who was Deqian; he was described as an "old distinguished scholar of Jiangnan" and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Hanlin bachelors completed their probation, the Qianlong Emperor visited in the late afternoon, asked which man was Deqian, heard him called "an old literary luminary of Jiangnan," and appointed him Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 出御製詩令賡和，稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an imperial poem and ordered matching verses; Deqian pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor produced one of his own poems and asked for a harmonizing response; Deqian's reply met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 八年，即擢中允，五遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was immediately promoted to middle attendant and was transferred five times to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promptly raised to middle attendant, and over five further transfers he rose to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乞假還葬，命不必開缺。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return home for a burial; he was ordered that his post need not be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for leave to go home and conduct a funeral, and was told his office did not have to be declared open.

sentences.zh: 德潛入辭，乞封父母，上命予三代封典，賦詩餞之。

translations.literal: Deqian entered to take leave, requested enfeoffment honors for his parents; the emperor ordered honors granted for three generations and composed a poem to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Deqian came to bid farewell and asked that honors be conferred on his parents, the emperor granted enfeoffment rites for three generations and wrote a parting poem for him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命在上書房行走，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to serve in the Upper Study and was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was assigned to duty in the Upper Study and promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上諭諸臣曰：「沈德潛誠實謹厚，且憐其晚遇，是以稠疊加恩，以勵老成積學之士，初不因進詩而優擢也。」

translations.literal: That year the emperor instructed the ministers, saying: "Shen Deqian is honest and cautious in character, and moreover I pity his late advancement; therefore I have repeatedly bestowed favor to encourage seasoned scholars of accumulated learning—it was not from the outset because of presenting poems that he was specially promoted."
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor told his ministers: "Shen Deqian is sincere, trustworthy, and steady in character. I also feel for how late in life he finally received office, which is why I have heaped favor upon him—to encourage elderly scholars who have long cultivated their learning. From the beginning his advancement was not a special promotion earned by submitting poems."

sentences.zh: 十三年，德潛以齒衰病噎乞休，命以原銜食俸，仍在上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Deqian, because of advanced age and a choking illness, requested retirement; he was ordered to receive salary at his original rank and still to serve in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Deqian asked to retire on account of his advanced age and a swallowing ailment. The emperor let him keep his original rank and salary and continue duty in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十四年，复乞歸，命原品休致，仍令校御製詩集畢乃行。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he again requested to return home; he was ordered to retire at his original rank, but still told to finish collating the imperial poetry collection before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he again asked to go home. He was permitted to retire at his existing rank, but only after he had completed proofreading the imperial poetry collection.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕於德潛，以詩始，以詩終。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "In my dealings with Deqian, it began with poetry and will end with poetry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him: "Between Deqian and me, everything began with poetry and will end with poetry."

sentences.zh: 且令有所著作，許寄京呈覽。

translations.literal: Moreover he was told that whatever writings he might produce were permitted to be sent to the capital for the emperor's review.
translations.idiomatic: He was also told that any future work he wrote might be sent to the capital for the emperor to read.

sentences.zh: 賜以人葠，賦詩寵其行。

translations.literal: He was granted ginseng, and a poem was composed to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him ginseng and wrote a poem to grace his journey home.

sentences.zh: 德潛歸，進所著歸愚集，上親為製序，稱其詩伯仲高、王，高、王者謂高啟、王士禎也。

translations.literal: Deqian returned home and submitted his own Guiyu Collection; the emperor personally wrote a preface, saying his poetry ranked alongside Gao and Wang—Gao and Wang meaning Gao Qi and Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Deqian went home he presented his Guiyu Collection. The emperor personally wrote its preface and declared his poetry the equal of Gao Qi and Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上南巡，命在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the emperor made a southern tour, Deqian was ordered to receive salary while remaining on native-place registration.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, during the emperor's southern tour, Deqian was granted salary while retaining his registered residence status.

sentences.zh: 是冬，德潛詣京師祝皇太后六十萬壽。

translations.literal: That winter Deqian went to the capital to congratulate the empress dowager on her sixtieth birthday.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Deqian traveled to the capital to offer birthday congratulations to the empress dowager on her sixtieth milestone.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，上召賜曲宴，賦雪獅與聯句。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year the emperor summoned him and granted a private banquet, composing on the snow lion and linked verses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year the emperor invited him to a private banquet and joined him in verses on a snow lion and in linked-verse composition.

sentences.zh: 又以德潛年八十，賜額曰「鶴性鬆身」，並賚藏佛、冠服。

translations.literal: Also, because Deqian was eighty years old, a plaque reading "Crane Nature, Pine Body" was bestowed, together with a funerary Buddha image and ceremonial cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Because Deqian had reached eighty, the emperor also granted him a plaque inscribed "Crane Nature, Pine Body," along with a Buddhist image for his death rites and formal cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 德潛歸，復進西湖志纂，上題三絕句代序。

translations.literal: Deqian returned and again submitted the Gazetteer of West Lake; the emperor inscribed three quatrains in place of a preface.
translations.idiomatic: When Deqian went home he again presented his compiled Gazetteer of West Lake, and the emperor supplied three quatrains to serve as its preface.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，复南巡，加禮部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor again made a southern tour, Deqian was given the brevet rank of minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, during another southern tour, he was granted the honorary title of minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，复詣京師祝皇太后七十萬壽，進歷代聖母圖冊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again went to the capital to congratulate the empress dowager on her seventieth birthday and submitted an illustrated compendium of sagely mothers through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he again traveled to the capital for the empress dowager's seventieth birthday and presented an illustrated album of exemplary mothers from successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 入朝賜杖，上命集文武大臣七十以上者為九老，凡三班，德潛為致仕九老首。

translations.literal: Upon entering court he was granted a ceremonial staff; the emperor ordered that civil and military ministers aged seventy or above be gathered as the Nine Elders, three groups in all, with Deqian as head of the retired Nine Elders.
translations.idiomatic: When he attended court he received a ceremonial staff. The emperor assembled civil and military officials aged seventy and above into three groups of Nine Elders, and Deqian was named chief among the retired elders.

sentences.zh: 命遊香山，圖形內府。

translations.literal: They were ordered to visit Fragrant Hills, and their likenesses were painted for the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The elders were sent on an excursion to Fragrant Hills, and portraits of them were kept in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 德潛進所編國朝詩別裁集請序，上覽其書以錢謙益為冠，因諭：「謙益諸人為明朝達官，而復事本朝，草昧締構，一時權宜。

translations.literal: Deqian submitted the Qing Poetry Separate Anthology he had compiled and requested a preface; the emperor, on reading the book, saw Qian Qianyi placed at the head, and therefore instructed: "Qianyi and men like him were high officials of the Ming, yet they again served this dynasty—at the founding amid chaos this was a temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Deqian presented his edited Separate Anthology of Qing Poetry and asked for an imperial preface. When the emperor read it and found Qian Qianyi ranked first, he said: "Qianyi and his kind were eminent Ming officials who later served our dynasty. In the disorder of founding a new regime, that was a temporary necessity.

sentences.zh: 要其人不得為忠孝，其詩自在，聽之可也。

translations.literal: Essentially such men cannot be regarded as loyal and filial; as for their poetry itself, it may be left as it is and listened to.
translations.idiomatic: As men they cannot be called loyal and filial, but their poems may stand on their own and be read without objection.

sentences.zh: 選以冠本朝諸人則不可。

translations.literal: To select him to head the men of this dynasty is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: To place him at the head of Qing poets, however, is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 錢名世者，皇考所謂'名教罪人'，更不宜入選。

translations.literal: As for Qian Mingshi, he is what my late father called an 'enemy of moral teaching,' and is even less fit for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Mingshi was the man my father, the Yongzheng Emperor, condemned as an 'enemy of moral teaching'; he is even less suitable for inclusion.

sentences.zh: 慎郡王，朕之叔父也，朕尚不忍名之。

translations.literal: Prince Shen is my uncle, and I myself still cannot bear to speak his name.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen is my uncle, and even I cannot bring myself to name him.

sentences.zh: 德潛豈宜直書其名？

translations.literal: How could Deqian properly write his name directly?
translations.idiomatic: How could Deqian have thought it proper to record that name outright?

sentences.zh: 至世次前後倒置，益不可枚舉。」

translations.literal: As for generations and sequence being reversed front and back, these too cannot be enumerated one by one."
translations.idiomatic: As for reversing the order of generations and ranks, the errors are too many even to list."

sentences.zh: 命內廷翰林重為校定。

translations.literal: He ordered the Hanlin scholars of the inner court to revise and correct it anew.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the inner-court Hanlin to revise the anthology completely.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，南巡，德潛及錢陳群迎駕常州，上賜詩，並稱為「大老」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, during a southern tour, Deqian and Qian Chenqun welcomed the imperial procession at Changzhou; the emperor bestowed poems and together called them "great elders."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, on a southern tour, Deqian and Qian Chenqun greeted the emperor at Changzhou. He granted them poems and hailed them both as "great elders."

sentences.zh: 三十年，复南巡，仍迎駕常州，加太子太傅，賜其孫維熙舉人。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the emperor again made a southern tour, they still welcomed the procession at Changzhou; Deqian was given grand tutor of the crown prince, and his grandson Weixi was granted the juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, on yet another southern tour, they again received the emperor at Changzhou. Deqian was made grand tutor of the crown prince, and his grandson Weixi was granted the rank of juren.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒，年九十七。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died, aged ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he died at the age of ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太師，祀賢良祠，諡文愨。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given grand preceptor of the crown prince, enshrined in the Worthy Elders Shrine, and granted the posthumous name Wenque.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand preceptor of the crown prince, given a place in the Worthy Elders Shrine, and granted the posthumous title Wenque.

sentences.zh: 御製詩為輓。

translations.literal: An imperial poem served as elegy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a poem as his elegy.

sentences.zh: 是時上命毀錢謙益詩集，下兩江總督高晉令察德潛家如有謙益詩文集，遵旨繳出。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor ordered the destruction of Qian Qianyi's poetry collection and sent instructions to Governor-General Gao Jin of the Two Jiangs to investigate Deqian's household; if any of Qianyi's poetry or prose collections were found, they were to be surrendered in accordance with the edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor ordered Qian Qianyi's collected poems destroyed and instructed Governor-General Gao Jin of the Two Jiangs to search Deqian's home and confiscate any of Qianyi's literary works found there.

sentences.zh: 會德潛卒，高晉奏德潛家並未藏謙益詩文集，事乃已。

translations.literal: It happened that Deqian died; Gao Jin memorialized that Deqian's household had not kept Qianyi's poetry and prose collections, and the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Deqian happened to die just then. Gao Jin reported that his household possessed no works by Qianyi, and the affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，東台縣民訐舉人徐述夔一柱樓集有悖逆語，上覽集前有德潛所為傳，稱其品行文章皆可為法，上不懌。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year a man of Dongtai County denounced juren Xu Shukui's Yizhulou Collection for rebellious language; the emperor, reading the preface written by Deqian praising his conduct and writings as models to follow, was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year a Dongtai County resident reported that juren Xu Shukui's Yizhulou Collection contained seditious passages. When the emperor read Deqian's biographical preface calling Xu's character and writings exemplary, he was offended.

sentences.zh: 下大學士九卿議，奪德潛贈官，罷祠削諡，僕其墓碑。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the grand secretaries and the nine ministers for deliberation; Deqian's posthumous office was stripped, his shrine worship was abolished and posthumous title removed, and his tomb stele was demolished.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the grand secretaries and nine ministers, who stripped Deqian of his posthumous rank, removed him from the shrine, revoked his posthumous title, and had his tomb stele overturned.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，御製懷舊詩，仍列德潛五詞臣末。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, in an imperial nostalgic poem, Deqian was still listed last among five literary ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year the emperor's own nostalgic poem still placed Deqian last among five literary ministers.

sentences.zh: 德潛少受詩法於吳江葉燮，自盛唐上追漢、魏，論次唐以後列朝詩為別裁集，以規矩示人。

translations.literal: Deqian in youth received instruction in poetry from Ye Xie of Wujiang; from the High Tang he traced upward to Han and Wei, arranged poetry of successive dynasties after Tang into a separate anthology, and set standards to show others.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Deqian studied poetry under Ye Xie of Wujiang. Working from High Tang back through Han and Wei, he arranged post-Tang verse from successive dynasties into his Separate Anthology and offered it as a model of proper standards.

sentences.zh: 承學者效之，自成宗派。

translations.literal: Those who inherited his learning imitated him and formed a school of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Followers who took up his method imitated him until a distinct school of poetry took shape.

sentences.zh: 金德瑛，字汝白，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Jin Deying, style name Rubai, was a native of Renhe, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Deying, whose style name was Rubai, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，廷對初置第六，高宗親擢第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Qianlong, in the palace examination he was initially placed sixth; the Qianlong Emperor personally elevated him to first and appointed him compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Having become a jinshi in the first year of Qianlong, he was first ranked sixth in the palace examination, but the Qianlong Emperor personally raised him to first place and appointed him Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 是歲舉博學鴻詞科，德瑛以薦徵，既入翰林，不更試。

translations.literal: That year the Erudite Letters examination was held; Deying was summoned by recommendation, and once he had entered the Hanlin he was not examined again.
translations.idiomatic: That year the special Erudite Letters examination was held. Deying had been nominated and summoned, and once he entered the Hanlin he was excused from sitting the exam again.

sentences.zh: 旋命南書房行走，充江南鄉試考官。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to serve in the Southern Study and appointed examiner for the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Southern Study and made chief examiner for the Jiangnan provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 德瑛以原籍休寧辭，不許。

translations.literal: Deying declined on the ground that his original native place was Xiuning; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Deying asked to be excused because his ancestral home was Xiuning, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 再遷右庶子。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to right vice director of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to right vice director of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 督江西學政。

translations.literal: He supervised educational administration in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed educational commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 任滿，上特諭「德瑛甚有操守，取士公明」，命留任。

translations.literal: When his term expired, the emperor specially instructed that "Deying has very strong integrity and selects scholars with fairness and clarity," and ordered him retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, the emperor personally remarked that "Deying is a man of strong integrity who selects candidates fairly and openly," and ordered him to remain in the post.

sentences.zh: 德瑛疏言：「翰林為儲才地，庶吉士宜求學有根柢，器量明達，庶可備他日任使。

translations.literal: Deying memorialized, saying: "The Hanlin is a place for storing talent; Hanlin bachelors should be sought who have learning with solid foundations and clear, broad capacity, so that they may be prepared for future appointment and use.
translations.idiomatic: Deying submitted a memorial arguing that "the Hanlin is a reservoir of talent, and bachelors should be chosen for solid learning and clear, generous character so they can be readied for future service.

sentences.zh: 每科命大臣教習，大臣政事甚繁，但能總大綱。

translations.literal: Each cohort is ordered to be instructed by a grand minister, but grand ministers' administrative affairs are very numerous and they can only grasp the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Each class is placed under a senior minister as instructor, but those ministers are overwhelmed with administrative business and can oversee only the broad outlines.

sentences.zh: 舊有分教例，但由掌院選任，時設時止。

translations.literal: There was formerly a precedent for subdivided instruction, but selection was by the academy chancellor and the practice was established at times and stopped at times.
translations.idiomatic: There had once been a system of divided instruction, but the chancellor chose the instructors and the arrangement was adopted and dropped intermittently.

sentences.zh: 乞令掌院於翰詹中擇品學優贍、資俸較深者引見，簡畀分教。」

translations.literal: He requested that the chancellor select from among Hanlin and Hanlin-attached officials those of superior character and learning with relatively senior rank and salary, present them for audience, and assign them to subdivided teaching."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the chancellor choose from the Hanlin and associated officials men of outstanding character and scholarship with relatively senior rank, have them presented to the throne, and appoint them to teach in subdivided classes."

sentences.zh: 得旨俞允。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 复四遷太常寺卿，命祭告山西諸行省帝王陵寢。

translations.literal: He was again transferred four times to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was ordered to perform sacrificial announcements at imperial tombs in the provinces of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After four further promotions he became minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was sent to offer ritual announcements at imperial tombs throughout Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「女​​媧氏陵寢殿塑女像，旁侍嬪御，民間奉為求嗣之神，實為黷褻。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "In the hall of the tomb shrine of Lady Nüwa a female statue is molded, with attendant consorts at the side; the common people revere it as a god for seeking heirs—this is in truth profane and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "At the tomb shrine of Lady Nüwa the hall contains a molded female figure with attendant consorts beside her. The people worship her as a deity of childbirth, which is truly a profanation of the sacred site.

sentences.zh: 請毀像立主。」

translations.literal: He requested that the statue be destroyed and a spirit tablet erected."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the image be removed and a spirit tablet installed in its place."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries were ordered to deliberate and carry out the proposal.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政。

translations.literal: He supervised educational administration in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed educational commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十九年，歲饑，上發帑治賑，而鄒、滕諸縣災尤重。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year there was famine; the emperor disbursed treasury funds for relief, but the counties of Zou, Teng, and others suffered especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year famine struck. The emperor released treasury funds for relief, yet the counties of Zou, Teng, and neighboring districts were hit hardest.

sentences.zh: 有司格於例限，不敢以請。

translations.literal: Local officials were constrained by statutory limits and did not dare to submit requests.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, bound by regulatory limits, did not dare to ask for additional aid.

sentences.zh: 德瑛任滿還京師，入對，具言狀，上特命展賑。

translations.literal: When Deying's term expired and he returned to the capital, he entered audience and fully reported the situation; the emperor specially ordered relief extended.
translations.idiomatic: When Deying's term ended and he returned to the capital, he reported the full situation at audience. The emperor specially ordered relief extended.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 充江西鄉試考官。

translations.literal: He served as examiner for the Jiangxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief examiner for the Jiangxi provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 使還，經徐州，時河決孫家集，微山湖暴漲，入運河，江南、山東連壤諸州縣被水。

translations.literal: Returning from his mission he passed through Xuzhou; at that time the Yellow River broke at Sunjiaji, Weishan Lake surged violently and entered the Grand Canal, and contiguous prefectures and counties of Jiangnan and Shandong were inundated.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed through Xuzhou just as the Yellow River burst at Sunjiaji. Weishan Lake swelled and poured into the Grand Canal, flooding adjoining districts in Jiangnan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 德瑛諮訪形勢，入陳於上前，上嘉德瑛誠實不欺。

translations.literal: Deying inquired into the situation, entered and reported before the emperor, and the emperor praised Deying's honesty without deception.
translations.idiomatic: Deying investigated conditions on the ground and reported them directly to the emperor, who praised his honest and unvarnished account.

sentences.zh: 旋命尚書劉統勳董治疏築。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered that Minister Liu Tongxun supervise dredging and construction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly put Minister Liu Tongxun in charge of dredging and embankment work.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，督順天學政，疏言：「八旗諸生遇歲試，輒稱病諉避，甚至病者多於與試者，請下八旗都統考覈。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he supervised educational administration in Shuntian and memorialized, saying: "Banner students, when the annual examination comes, repeatedly claim illness to evade it; indeed the sick sometimes outnumber those who take the exam—I request that the banner commanders be ordered to investigate."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as Shuntian educational commissioner, he memorialized: "When the annual examinations come, banner students routinely plead illness to avoid them—sometimes more claim sickness than actually sit the exam. I ask that the banner commanders be ordered to investigate."

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢左都御史，疏言：「秋審舊例，凡已經秋審者謂之'舊事'，現入秋審者謂之'新事'。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to left censor-in-chief and memorialized, saying: "Under the old autumn review practice, cases already reviewed in autumn review are called 'old cases,' and cases newly entering autumn review are called 'new cases.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made left censor-in-chief and wrote: "Under the autumn review rules, cases already reviewed are called 'old cases,' while those newly entering review are called 'new cases.'

sentences.zh: 當九卿、詹事、科道集議時，書吏宣唱名冊，繁重淹滯。

translations.literal: When the nine ministers, Hanlin academicians, and censorial officials gather for joint deliberation, clerks read aloud the name registers—a heavy, obstructive delay.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine ministers, academicians, and censorial officials meet to deliberate, clerks read the name registers aloud, a cumbersome process that bogs proceedings down.

sentences.zh: 其實商榷輕重，多在新事。

translations.literal: In fact the discussion weighing severity falls mostly on new cases.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, most of the debate over sentencing severity concerns new cases.

sentences.zh: 積年緩決之案，自按察使上巡撫，更三法司，初獄已致慎矣；

translations.literal: Cases deferred for decision over accumulated years, from the provincial surveillance commissioner up through the governor, and through the three judicial offices, were already handled with caution at the initial trial;
translations.idiomatic: Cases deferred year after year have already passed from the surveillance commissioner to the governor and through the three judicial offices, and the original trials were conducted with great care;

sentences.zh: 況三審緩決，久成信讞。

translations.literal: moreover, after three reviews with deferred decision, they have long become established verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, after three rounds of review with deferred execution, they have long since become settled verdicts.

sentences.zh: 諸囚偷生囹圄，幸待十年慶典，得蒙恩赦。

translations.literal: The various prisoners cling to life in prison, hoping to await the decennial celebration and receive imperial amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners linger in their cells, gambling on the decennial celebration in hopes of imperial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 然亦裁自聖心，諸臣無與焉。

translations.literal: Yet that too is decided from the sacred mind; the various ministers have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet amnesty rests solely with the emperor's own judgment; the ministers play no part in it.

sentences.zh: 舊事名冊宜罷宣唱。

translations.literal: The name register of old cases should cease to be read aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The register of old cases should no longer be read aloud.

sentences.zh: 陳案既省，近事得以從容往復，盡心詳審。

translations.literal: Once stale cases are reduced, recent cases can be discussed back and forth at leisure and examined in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: With old cases set aside, recent ones can be debated at length and reviewed thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 九卿兼有餘晷治其本職。」

translations.literal: The nine ministers would also have remaining hours to attend to their regular duties."
translations.idiomatic: The nine ministers would also have time left to handle their regular responsibilities."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言，下大學士會刑部議，請如德瑛言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and sent the matter to the grand secretaries to confer with the Ministry of Punishments; they requested action as Deying had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed his proposal and referred it to the grand secretaries and the Ministry of Punishments, who recommended adopting Deying's plan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命稽覈通州倉儲，中寒病作，二十七年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was ordered to audit grain stores at Tongzhou; he was stricken with a cold illness, and in the first month of the twenty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was assigned to audit Tongzhou granaries, fell ill with a chill, and died in the first month of the twenty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 德瑛端平簡直，無有偏黨，為上所知。

translations.literal: Deying was upright, even, straightforward, and without partisan bias, and was known to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Deying was even-tempered, upright, and free of faction, and the emperor held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 方為少詹事，入對，上曰：「汝元年狀元，尚作四品官耶？」

translations.literal: When he was junior tutor of the heir apparent and entered audience, the emperor said: "You were top laureate of the first year—are you still holding a fourth-rank office?"
translations.idiomatic: While he was still junior tutor of the heir apparent, the emperor asked at audience: "You were the top jinshi of the first year of my reign—are you still only a fourth-rank official?"

sentences.zh: 數日擢太常寺卿。

translations.literal: Within several days he was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及病，上每見廷臣問狀，且曰：「德瑛辛巳生，長朕十歲。」

translations.literal: When he fell ill, whenever the emperor saw court ministers he asked after his condition, and said: "Deying was born in the xinsi year and is ten years older than I."
translations.idiomatic: When he grew ill, the emperor asked court ministers about his condition whenever he saw them, remarking: "Deying was born in the xinsi year and is ten years my senior."

sentences.zh: 及病革，上方出巡幸，將啟蹕，猶曰：「德瑛久不入值，病必重。」

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, the emperor was on tour and about to set out; he still said: "Deying has long not reported for duty—his illness must be grave."
translations.idiomatic: As his illness turned critical, the emperor was away on tour and about to depart, yet still said: "Deying has not reported for duty in some time—his illness must be serious."

sentences.zh: 德瑛即以其日卒。

translations.literal: Deying died that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Deying died that same day.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，德瑛子潔成進士，引見，上曰：「汝金德瑛子耶？」

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Deying's son Jiecheng became a jinshi; at presentation to the throne the emperor said: "Are you the son of Jin Deying?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Deying's son Jiecheng passed the jinshi examination. At his audience the emperor asked: "Are you Jin Deying's son?"

sentences.zh: 德瑛卒已將十年，上猶惓惓如是。

translations.literal: Deying had already been dead nearly ten years, yet the emperor was still so affectionately mindful.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten years after Deying's death, the emperor still remembered him with such warmth.

sentences.zh: 錢載，字坤一，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Qian Zai, style name Kunyi, was a native of Xiushui, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zai, whose style name was Kunyi, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年，副榜貢生，舉博學鴻詞、舉經學，就試皆未入選。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he was a tribute student on the supplementary list; he was nominated for the Erudite Letters and Classical Learning examinations and sat for both, but was not selected in either.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he graduated as a tribute student on the supplementary list. Nominated for the Erudite Letters and Classical Learning examinations, he competed in both but was not chosen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 七遷內閣學士，直上書房。

translations.literal: Through seven transfers he rose to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat and served directly in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: After seven promotions he reached grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat and served in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，督山東學政。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he supervised educational administration in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was appointed educational commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，命祭告陝西、四川岳瀆及帝王陵寢。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was ordered to perform sacrificial announcements at the sacred mountains and rivers of Shaanxi and Sichuan and at imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was sent to offer ritual announcements at the sacred peaks and rivers of Shaanxi and Sichuan and at imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部侍郎，充江南鄉試考官，舉顧問為第一，四書文純用排偶，上以乖文體，命議處。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice minister of rites and served as examiner for the Jiangnan provincial examination; he placed Gu Wen first, but his Four Books essay used parallel prose throughout—the emperor, holding that this violated literary form, ordered disciplinary deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of rites and chief examiner for the Jiangnan provincial examinations. He ranked Gu Wen first, but Gu's Four Books essay was written entirely in parallel couplets. The emperor judged this a breach of proper literary form and ordered disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 呂氏春秋堯葬穀林，史記不書其地。

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu records that Yao was buried at Gulin; the Records of the Grand Historian does not note the place.
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu says Yao was buried at Gulin, but the Records of the Grand Historian gives no location for the burial.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以山東巡撫岳濬奏，自東平改祀濮州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, on the memorial of Shandong governor Yue Jun, the site of sacrifice was moved from Dongping to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, on the recommendation of the governor of Shandong, Yue Jun, the rites were transferred from Dongping to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，大理寺卿尹嘉銓疏言當在平陽，下部議駁。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Yin Jiaquan, memorialized that the site ought to be at Pingyang; the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year Yin Jiaquan, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, argued in a memorial that the tomb should be at Pingyang, but after referral to the ministries the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 載督學山東，謁濮州堯陵，自四川還道平陽，得堯陵州東北；

translations.literal: When Zai supervised education in Shandong he visited Yao's tomb at Puzhou; returning from Sichuan he passed through Pingyang and found Yao's tomb northeast of the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: While serving as educational commissioner of Shandong, Zai paid his respects at the tomb of Yao at Puzhou; on his return from Sichuan he traveled by way of Pingyang and located the tomb northeast of the prefectural seat;

sentences.zh: 及江南典試歸，又至東平求舊時所祭堯陵，參互考訂，以為在平陽者是。

translations.literal: When he returned from presiding over the Jiangnan provincial examination he again went to Dongping to seek the tomb of Yao formerly worshipped there; comparing and verifying the evidence, he concluded that the one at Pingyang was correct.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from chief examining duty in Jiangnan, he went again to Dongping to find the tomb of Yao that had once been worshipped there; cross-checking the evidence, he concluded that the site at Pingyang was the true one.

sentences.zh: 史記湯、武皆未著葬地，蓋都於是葬於是則不書，堯亦其例。

translations.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian records no burial place for Tang or Wu—presumably because when one ruled and was buried in the same place it was not written down; Yao follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Grand Historian gives no burial place for Tang or Wu, presumably because when a ruler reigned and was buried in the same locale the historian did not record it; Yao follows that same convention.

sentences.zh: 因疏請釐定。

translations.literal: Accordingly he memorialized requesting a definitive ruling.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial asking that the site be authoritatively fixed.

sentences.zh: 下大學士、九卿議駁，載奏辨；

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the nine chief ministers for deliberation and rejection; Zai memorialized in rebuttal;
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the grand secretaries and the nine chief ministers, who rejected his claim; Zai answered with a counter-memorial;

sentences.zh: 复議，仍寢不行。

translations.literal: On further deliberation the proposal was again shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: After further review the proposal was once again set aside.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「經生論古，反覆辨證，原所不禁。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "When classicists discuss antiquity and argue back and forth in proof, that is not forbidden in itself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When scholars of the classics debate antiquity and argue their cases at length, I have never forbidden it.

sentences.zh: 但既陳之奏牘，並經廷臣集議，即不當再執成見。

translations.literal: But once it has been set forth in a memorial and has already been jointly deliberated by court ministers, one ought not cling stubbornly to a fixed view.
translations.idiomatic: But once a view has been laid before the throne in a memorial and the court has deliberated together, one should not cling stubbornly to one's original opinion.

sentences.zh: 載斥呂不韋門下客浮說，不韋即不足取，亦尚不可以人廢言。

translations.literal: Zai denounced the empty talk of Lü Buwei's retainers; even if Lü Buwei himself is not worth taking seriously, one still may not reject a statement because of the man who made it.
translations.idiomatic: Zai dismissed the writings of Lü Buwei's retainers as empty speculation; even if Lü Buwei himself is unworthy of esteem, one still must not dismiss a statement solely because of who wrote it.

sentences.zh: 況其門下客所著書，所謂'懸之國門，不易一字'，豈能謂不足為據？

translations.literal: Moreover, the book written by his retainers—the one said to be such that 'if hung at the state gate, not a word would be changed'—how can one say it is not sufficient to serve as evidence?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the book produced by those retainers was of the sort they claimed could be hung at the state gate without changing a single word—how can one say it affords no basis for judgment?

sentences.zh: 其時去古未遠，或尚有所承述。

translations.literal: That age was not far removed from antiquity, and may still have preserved transmitted accounts.
translations.idiomatic: That time was not far removed from antiquity, and may still have preserved reliable traditions.

sentences.zh: 乃欲在數千年後虛揣翻駁，有是理乎？

translations.literal: Yet one would wish, thousands of years later, to overturn it by empty conjecture—is there any sense in that?
translations.idiomatic: To overturn it thousands of years later on the basis of idle speculation—is that reasonable?

sentences.zh: 載本晚達，且其事只是考古，是以不加深問。

translations.literal: Zai had in any case achieved office late in life, and the matter concerned only the study of antiquity, so the emperor did not press the inquiry further.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had come to office late in any case, and the matter concerned only archaeological scholarship, so the emperor did not pursue it further.

sentences.zh: 若遇朝廷政治，亦似此嘵嘵不已，朕必重治其罪。」

translations.literal: If in matters of court governance he were likewise to chatter on without cease, I would certainly punish his offense severely."
translations.idiomatic: If he were to carry on like this over matters of state policy, I would certainly punish him severely."

sentences.zh: 命傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: He ordered that the instruction be transmitted to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: He had an edict delivered to reprimand him.

sentences.zh: 載疏累數千言，語有未明，復為自註，時謂非章奏體，上亦未深詰也。

translations.literal: Zai's memorial ran to several thousand words; where the language was unclear he added his own annotations, and contemporaries said this was not proper memorial form, yet the emperor did not press the matter deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's memorial ran to several thousand words; where his meaning was obscure he added explanatory notes of his own, which contemporaries judged improper for an official memorial, but the emperor did not pursue the point.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，休致。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，卒，年八十有五。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died, at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he died, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 子世錫，入翰林。

translations.literal: His son Shixi entered the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixi was appointed to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎英廉及載充教習庶吉士，英廉語世錫曰：「君家仍世入翰林，而上命父教其子，當勉為朅、頲以報上恩。」

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister Ying Lian and Zai served as instructors to the Hanlin bachelors; Ying Lian said to Shixi: "Your family has for generations entered the Hanlin, and the emperor has ordered the father to teach the son—you should strive to emulate Xie and Ting to repay the imperial grace."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Minister Ying Lian and Zai were serving as instructors to the Hanlin bachelors; Ying Lian told Shixi: "Your family has produced Hanlin scholars for generations, and now the emperor has appointed your father to instruct his own son—you should strive to match the example of Xie and Ting and repay the emperor's favor."

sentences.zh: 世錫子寶甫，初名昌齡，避仁宗陵，以字行。

translations.literal: Shixi's son Baofu was originally named Changling; to avoid the taboo on the name of the Jiaqing Emperor's tomb he was known by his style name.
