translations.idiomatic: Shixi's son Baofu had originally been named Changling; to avoid the taboo associated with the Jiaqing Emperor's tomb name, he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 亦以編修官至雲南布政使。

translations.literal: He likewise rose from compiler to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He too rose from compiler to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 德瑛論詩宗黃庭堅，謂當辭必己出，不主故常。

translations.literal: Deying in discussing poetry took Huang Tingjian as his master, holding that one's wording must come from oneself and should not adhere to old conventions.
translations.idiomatic: In his poetics Deying looked to Huang Tingjian, insisting that language must be one's own and must not cling to received formulas.

sentences.zh: 載初與訂交，晚登第，乃為門下門生；

translations.literal: Zai at first formed a friendship with him; having passed the examinations late, he became a disciple under his patronage;
translations.idiomatic: Zai had first become his friend; after passing the examinations late in life, he became a disciple under his tutelage;

sentences.zh: 詩亦宗庭堅，險入橫出，嶄然成一家。

translations.literal: His poetry likewise took Tingjian as its model—entering perilous ground and breaking out sideways—standing forth as a school of its own.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry likewise followed Tingjian, daring and unexpected, until it stood forth as a distinctive school in its own right.

sentences.zh: 同縣王又曾、萬光泰輩相與唱酬，號秀水派。

translations.literal: With fellow natives Wang Youceng, Wan Guangtai, and others he exchanged poems in mutual response, and they were called the Xiushui school.
translations.idiomatic: Together with fellow townsmen Wang Youceng, Wan Guangtai, and others he exchanged poems in fellowship, and they were known as the Xiushui school.

sentences.zh: 語互詳文苑傳。

translations.literal: Their story is told in detail in the Biographies of Literary Men.
translations.idiomatic: Their careers are recounted at length in the Biographies of Literary Men.

sentences.zh: 載又為陳群族孫，從陳群母陳受畫法，蒼秀高勁，亦如其詩。

translations.literal: Zai was also a clansman of Chen Qun on his mother's side; he studied painting under Chen Qun's mother, Lady Chen, and his work was austere, elegant, and forceful—like his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was also related to Chen Qun through his mother's clan; he studied painting under Chen Qun's mother, Lady Chen, and his brushwork was spare, refined, and vigorous—much like his verse.

sentences.zh: 齊召南，字次風，浙江天台人。

translations.literal: Qi Zhaonan, style name Cifeng, was a native of Tiantai, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhaonan, whose style name was Cifeng, came from Tiantai in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼而穎敏，鄉里稱神童。

translations.literal: From childhood he was keen and quick, and his home district called him a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was exceptionally bright, and his neighbors hailed him as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，命舉博學鴻詞，召南以副榜貢生被薦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng an order went out to nominate candidates for Erudite Letters; Zhaonan, a tribute student on the supplementary list, was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng the throne called for nominations to the Erudite Letters examination, and Zhaonan, a tribute student on the supplementary list, was put forward.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，廷試二等，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he placed in the second rank at the palace examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he placed second class in the palace examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after completing his term was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 八年，禦試翰詹各官，擢中允，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor tested all Hanlin and Hanlin Academy officials; Zhaonan was promoted to middle attendant and transferred to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor examined the Hanlin and Academy officials; Zhaonan was promoted to middle attendant and then to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 九年，以父喪去官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he left office to observe mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 時方校刻經史，召南分撰禮記、漢書考證，命即家撰進。

translations.literal: At the time the classics and histories were being collated and carved for printing; Zhaonan was assigned to compile textual notes on the Record of Rites and the Book of Han, and was ordered to draft and submit them from home.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then collating and printing the classics and histories; Zhaonan was assigned to compile textual studies for the Record of Rites and the Book of Han and was told to draft and submit his work from home.

sentences.zh: 服除，起原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to bachelor reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made bachelor reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復試翰詹各官，以召南列首，擢內閣學士，命上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Hanlin and Academy officials were tested again; Zhaonan ranked first and was promoted to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat, with orders to serve in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Hanlin and Academy officials were examined again; Zhaonan ranked first and was promoted to grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat and assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 上於寧古塔得古鏡，問召南，召南辨其款識，具陳原委。

translations.literal: The emperor obtained an ancient mirror at Ningguta and questioned Zhaonan; Zhaonan identified its inscription and fully explained its provenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acquired an ancient mirror at Ningguta and asked Zhaonan about it; Zhaonan read its inscription and explained its history in full.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「是不愧博學鴻詞矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those beside him and said: "This truly befits one selected for Erudite Letters!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to those around him and said: "This is worthy indeed of an Erudite Letters scholar!"

sentences.zh: 上西苑射，發十九矢皆中的，顧尚書蔣溥及召南曰：「不可無詩！」

translations.literal: The emperor went shooting in the Western Park; of nineteen arrows he loosed, all hit the mark. He turned to Minister Jiang Pu and Zhaonan and said: "There must be a poem!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went shooting in the Western Park and hit the mark with all nineteen arrows. He turned to Minister Jiang Pu and Zhaonan and said: "We must have a poem for this!"

sentences.zh: 召南進詩，上和以賜。

translations.literal: Zhaonan presented a poem; the emperor wrote a reply and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaonan offered a poem, and the emperor composed a matching verse and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，召南散直墮馬，觸大石，顱幾裂。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year, after leaving duty at the palace, Zhaonan fell from his horse, struck a large rock, and nearly split his skull.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year, after leaving the palace at the end of his shift, Zhaonan fell from his horse, struck a boulder, and nearly split his skull open.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣蒙古醫就視，賜以藥。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sent a Mongol physician to attend him and bestowed medicine.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of the accident, the emperor sent a Mongol physician to treat him and granted him medicine.

sentences.zh: 語皇子宏適：「汝師傅病如何？

translations.literal: He told the prince Hongshi: "How is your tutor's illness?
translations.idiomatic: He told Prince Hongshi: "How is your tutor's illness?

sentences.zh: 當頻使存問！」

translations.literal: You must send inquiries frequently!"
translations.idiomatic: You must inquire after him often!"

sentences.zh: 幸木蘭，使賜鹿脯十五束。

translations.literal: On an excursion to Mulan he had fifteen bundles of venison sent as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunting trip to Mulan he sent Zhaonan fifteen bundles of venison as a gift.

sentences.zh: 及冬，入謝，上慰勞，召南因乞歸，固請乃許。

translations.literal: When winter came he entered the capital to give thanks; the emperor comforted him, and Zhaonan thereupon begged to return home—only after repeated pleading was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he came to the capital to offer thanks; the emperor comforted him, and Zhaonan asked to retire home—only after he pressed his request repeatedly was he allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 及行，賜紗、葛各二端。

translations.literal: When he departed he was granted two bolts each of gauze and ramie cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, the emperor bestowed on him two bolts each of gauze and ramie.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，屢迎駕，輒問病狀，出御製詩命和。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the south, Zhaonan repeatedly welcomed the imperial procession; each time the emperor asked after his illness and produced an imperial poem ordering a matching verse.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour Zhaonan repeatedly welcomed the imperial procession; the emperor each time asked after his health and presented an imperial poem for him to match in reply.

sentences.zh: 上嘗詢天台、雁宕兩山景物，召南對未嘗遊覽。

translations.literal: The emperor once inquired about the scenery of Mount Tiantai and Mount Yandang; Zhaonan replied that he had never visited them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked about the scenery of Mount Tiantai and Mount Yandang; Zhaonan answered that he had never seen them.

sentences.zh: 上問：「名勝在鄉里間，何以不往？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Famous sites lie within your home district—why have you not gone to see them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "These famous places are right in your home country—why have you never visited them?"

sentences.zh: 召南對：「山峻溪深，臣有老母，怵古人登高臨深之誡，是以未敢往。」

translations.literal: Zhaonan replied: "The mountains are steep and the streams deep; I have an aged mother, and I shrink before the ancients' warning against looking down from heights and peering into depths, and so have not ventured there."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaonan answered: "The mountains are steep and the ravines deep; I have an aged mother, and I heed the ancient warning against standing on high places and looking into deep ones, and so I have not dared to go."

sentences.zh: 上深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 既而，以族人周華為書訕上，逮詣京師，吏議坐隱匿，當流，籍其家，上命奪職放歸，還其產十三四。

translations.literal: Before long, because his clansman Zhou Hua had written a book slandering the emperor, Zhaonan was seized and brought to the capital; the officials held that he was guilty of concealment and deserved banishment, with confiscation of his household; the emperor ordered that his office be stripped and that he be sent home, restoring three or four tenths of his property.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward his clansman Zhou Hua was found to have written a book slandering the emperor; Zhaonan was brought to the capital, and the officials judged him guilty of concealment and recommended exile and confiscation of his estate. The emperor stripped him of office and sent him home, restoring only three or four tenths of his property.

sentences.zh: 召南歸，遂卒。

translations.literal: Zhaonan returned home and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaonan returned home and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 召南易直子諒，文辭渰雅。

translations.literal: Zhaonan was candid and upright, his style unassuming, and his writing refined and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaonan was plainspoken and upright, his manner unpretentious, and his prose refined and graceful.

sentences.zh: 著水道提綱，具詳源委脈絡；

translations.literal: He authored the Essentials of Waterways, setting forth in full the sources, courses, and connections of rivers;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Essentials of Waterways, tracing rivers from their sources through their full courses;

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王年表，舉諸史綱要：並行於世。

translations.literal: and Chronological Tables of Emperors Through the Ages, summarizing the essentials of the various histories: both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: and Chronological Tables of Emperors Through the Ages, distilling the main lines of the dynastic histories—both works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 陈兆崙，字星齋，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhaolun, style name Xingzhai, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhaolun, whose style name was Xingzhai, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 亦幼慧。

translations.literal: He too was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: He too showed exceptional talent as a child.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年進士，福建即用知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he became a jinshi and was appointed directly as magistrate in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed at once as a county magistrate in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 舉博學鴻詞，詣京師試，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: Nominated for Erudite Letters, he went to the capital for the examination, was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated for the Erudite Letters examination, he traveled to the capital to compete, was appointed a Grand Secretariat secretary, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，廷試二等，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he placed in the second rank at the palace examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he placed second class in the palace examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上御經筵，以撰進講義稱旨，擢左中允。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor presided over the Classics Lectern; because the lecture notes Zhaolun drafted and submitted pleased him, he was promoted to left middle attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor attended the Classics Lectern; the lecture notes Zhaolun drafted and submitted pleased him, and he was promoted to left middle attendant.

sentences.zh: 禦試翰詹各官，复擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor tested the Hanlin and Academy officials, he was again promoted to bachelor lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's examination of Hanlin and Academy officials, he was further promoted to bachelor lecturer.

sentences.zh: 再遷順天府府尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to governor of Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed governor of Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 值大水，兆崙心計指畫，撫綏安集，無不得所。

translations.literal: When a great flood struck, Zhaolun devised plans in his mind and directed relief; in comforting and settling the people, none failed to find proper aid.
translations.idiomatic: During a major flood Zhaolun planned and directed relief with clear judgment; in comforting and resettling the people, he left no one without proper care.

sentences.zh: 畿輔役繁，舊設官車疲敝，議僉富戶應役，兆崙奏罷之。

translations.literal: Labor service in the capital region was heavy; the official carts long established were worn out, and there was a proposal that wealthy households be conscripted for the duty—Zhaolun memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Labor levies in the capital region were burdensome; the official transport carts had fallen into disrepair, and some proposed drafting wealthy households to serve instead—Zhaolun memorialized to have the scheme abolished.

sentences.zh: 時方西征，發禁旅，兆崙經畫宿頓儲蓄，井井有緒，軍民晏然。

translations.literal: At the time a western campaign was under way and the palace guard was mobilized; Zhaolun organized encampments and stores in orderly fashion, and army and people alike remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: A western campaign was then under way and the palace guard had been mobilized; Zhaolun organized encampments and supplies with meticulous order, and both soldiers and civilians remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to chief steward of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed chief steward of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上謁陵，以同官迎駕失儀，左授太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the imperial tombs, Zhaolun's fellow official failed in propriety while welcoming the imperial procession, and Zhaolun was demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to the tombs, a colleague failed in propriety while receiving the procession, and Zhaolun was demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 再遷太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-sixth year.

sentences.zh: 兆崙精六書之學，尤長經義，於易、書、禮均有論述。

translations.literal: Zhaolun was accomplished in the study of the Six Scripts and especially excelled in classical exegesis; on the Changes, Documents, and Rites he had treatises in each.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolun mastered the study of the Six Scripts and was especially skilled in classical exegesis; he wrote on the Changes, the Documents, and the Rites.

sentences.zh: 為詩文澹泊清遠。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were plain, restrained, clear, and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were spare, serene, and luminous.

sentences.zh: 孫桂生，字堅木。

translations.literal: Sun Guisheng, style name Jianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guisheng, whose style name was Jianmu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，自優貢生授知縣，揀發湖北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign he was appointed magistrate from the ranks of outstanding tribute students and was selected for assignment to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiaqing reign he was appointed county magistrate from among outstanding tribute students and was posted to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時教匪為亂，桂生從廣州將軍明亮擊賊，破孝感，殲魯惟志；

translations.literal: At the time the Teaching Sect rebels were in revolt; Guisheng followed the Guangzhou general Mingliang in attacking the bandits, broke Xiaogan, and destroyed Lu Weizhi;
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus rebels rose in revolt, Guisheng followed General Mingliang of Guangzhou against them, captured Xiaogan, and killed Lu Weizhi;

sentences.zh: 戰歸州，禦齊王氏：屢有功。

translations.literal: He fought at Guizhou and held off Qi Lady Wang, winning repeated merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Guizhou against the rebel leader Qi Lady Wang and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 授大冶知縣，再遷安陸知府。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Daye and was twice promoted to prefect of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Daye and later promoted to prefect of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 九年，遭母喪，湖北巡撫章煦疏請留軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when his mother died, Hubei governor Zhang Xu memorialized requesting that he be kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, while mourning his mother, he was kept with the army at the request of the governor of Hubei, Zhang Xu.

sentences.zh: 喪終，除荊州知府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三遷，再轉為江寧布政使，署江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: Through three promotions and two further transfers he became provincial treasurer of Jiangning and served concurrently as governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions and two further transfers he became provincial treasurer of Jiangning and served concurrently as acting governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡劾桂生徵賦不力，奪職；

translations.literal: Chu Pengling impeached Guisheng for insufficient effort in tax collection, and his office was stripped;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pengling impeached Guisheng for lax tax collection, and he was dismissed from office;

sentences.zh: 复劾察庫帑不實，上命大學士托津、戶部尚書景安按治，疏言：「桂生察庫帑無弊，徵賦亦逾十之七。」

translations.literal: He impeached him again for presenting a false accounting of treasury funds; the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Tuo Jin and Minister of Revenue Jing'an to investigate. They memorialized: "Guisheng's inspection found no irregularities in the treasury accounts, and tax collection had exceeded seven-tenths of the quota."
translations.idiomatic: Chu then impeached him again for falsifying the treasury accounts; the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Tuo Jin and Minister of Revenue Jing'an to investigate. They reported: "Guisheng's audit found no fraud in the treasury, and tax collection had exceeded seventy percent of the quota."

sentences.zh: 召詣京師，旋授甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital and soon appointed provincial treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and soon made provincial treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 再轉，复遷江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: After another transfer he was again promoted to governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After a further transfer he was again appointed governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 上六十萬壽，蠲各行省民間逋賦。

translations.literal: On the emperor's sixtieth birthday, unpaid popular levies in each province were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's sixtieth birthday, unpaid popular taxes throughout the provinces were remitted.

sentences.zh: 桂生疏言：「曠典殊施，當令澤及於民。

translations.literal: Guisheng memorialized: "This extraordinary grace and special measure ought to let its bounty reach the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Guisheng memorialized: "This extraordinary act of grace should truly reach the common people.

sentences.zh: 請自嘉慶元年起至二十二年，詳察民間逋賦，毋令官吏因緣為奸。

translations.literal: I ask that unpaid popular levies from the first year of Jiaqing through the twenty-second be examined in detail, so that officials may not exploit the occasion for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that unpaid popular taxes from the first year of Jiaqing through the twenty-second be examined in detail, so that officials may not use the remission as a pretext for corruption.

sentences.zh: 二十二年漕項，例至二十四年奏銷，民逋請並蠲除。」

translations.literal: Grain transport levies for the twenty-second year are routinely cleared through accounts in the twenty-fourth; unpaid popular levies should likewise be remitted entirely."
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport quotas for the twenty-second year are not routinely cleared until the twenty-fourth; unpaid popular levies in that category should be remitted as well."

sentences.zh: 又言：「民間逋賦有由州縣移他款代納者，今既蠲逋，當令現任州縣期十年償所移款。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Some unpaid popular levies were covered by counties and prefectures from other funds; now that arrears are remitted, current county and prefectural officials should be given ten years to repay the diverted sums."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Where counties and prefectures had covered unpaid popular taxes from other funds, current officials should be allowed ten years to repay those diverted sums now that the arrears are remitted."

sentences.zh: 皆議行。

translations.literal: All were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All his proposals were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 命署蘇州織造，兼領滸墅關，兼署兩江總督。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as superintendent of the Suzhou Weaving Office, to oversee also the Hushu Pass, and to serve concurrently as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting superintendent of the Suzhou Weaving Office, given concurrent charge of the Hushu customs station, and assigned to serve concurrently as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，召詣京師，以三品京堂待缺，旋命休致。

translations.literal: When the Daoguang Emperor ascended the throne, Guisheng was summoned to the capital and held a third-rank Capital Court post awaiting assignment; he was soon ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoguang Emperor came to the throne, Guisheng was summoned to the capital and given a third-rank Capital Court appointment pending assignment; he was soon ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year of the Daoguang reign.

sentences.zh: 桂生子憲曾，進士，官至詹事。

translations.literal: Guisheng's son Xianzeng became a jinshi and rose to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Guisheng's son Xianzeng passed the jinshi examination and rose to serve as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 董邦達，字孚存，浙江富陽人。

translations.literal: Dong Bangda, style name Fucun, was a native of Fuyang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Bangda, whose style name was Fucun, came from Fuyang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，選拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was selected as a tribute student through the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was selected as a tribute student through the special examination.

sentences.zh: 以尚書勵廷儀薦，命在戶部七品小京官上行走。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Minister Li Tingyi, he was ordered to serve as an attendant among the seventh-rank minor capital officials at the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Minister Li Tingyi, he was ordered to serve as an attendant among the Board of Revenue's seventh-rank minor capital officials.

sentences.zh: 十一年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，充陝西鄉試考官，疏言官卷數少，以民卷補中，報聞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he served as examiner for the Shaanxi provincial examination, memorialized that official examination papers were too few and that commoner papers should be used to fill the quota, and the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong he served as examiner for the Shaanxi provincial examination and memorialized that too few official examination papers had been submitted and that commoner papers should be used to fill the quota; the memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 授右中允，再遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Assistant Master of the Household and was promoted again to Reader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Assistant Master of the Household and was later promoted to Reader of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命直南書房，擢內閣學士，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to serve in the Southern Library, was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and returned home to observe mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was ordered to serve in the Southern Library and was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat; he then returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召詣京師，命視梁詩正例，入直食俸。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned to the capital and ordered, following Liang Shizheng's precedent, to resume service and draw his salary.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned to the capital and ordered, following Liang Shizheng's precedent, to resume active service and draw his salary.

sentences.zh: 十五年，補原官，遷侍郎，歷戶、工、吏諸部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was restored to his former post, promoted to vice minister, and served successively in the Boards of Revenue, Works, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was restored to his former post, promoted to vice minister, and served successively in the Boards of Revenue, Works, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，調還工​​部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred back to the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was transferred back to the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，仍調還禮部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was transferred back again to the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was transferred back again to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，以老病乞解任，上諭曰：「邦達年逾七十，衰病乞休，自合引年之例。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, citing old age and illness, he requested dismissal from office. The emperor instructed: "Bangda is over seventy and asks leave because of debility and illness; this accords with the precedent for retiring at advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, citing old age and illness, he asked to be relieved of office. The emperor instructed: "Bangda is over seventy and seeks retirement on account of debility and illness; this accords with the precedent for retiring at advanced age.

sentences.zh: 惟邦達移家京師，不能即還裡。

translations.literal: Only Bangda has moved his household to the capital and cannot immediately return home.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bangda has moved his household to the capital and cannot return home at once.

sentences.zh: 禮部事不繁，給假安心調治，不必解任。」

translations.literal: The business of the Board of Rites is not heavy; grant him leave to recuperate in peace without requiring him to resign."
translations.idiomatic: The business of the Board of Rites is not heavy; grant him leave to recuperate in peace without requiring him to resign his post."

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡文恪。

translations.literal: Imperial sacrifices and funeral honors were granted, and he was posthumously titled Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sacrifices and funeral honors were granted, and he was posthumously given the title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 邦達工山水，蒼逸古厚。

translations.literal: Bangda was skilled in landscape painting; his style was vigorous yet ancient and substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Bangda was skilled in landscape painting, his manner vigorous, unfettered, ancient, and substantial.

sentences.zh: 論者謂三董相承，為畫家正軌，目源、其昌與邦達也。

translations.literal: Critics say three generations of Dongs formed the orthodox lineage of painters, pointing to Yuan, Qichang, and Bangda.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that three generations of Dongs formed the orthodox lineage of painters, naming Dong Yuan, Dong Qichang, and Bangda.

sentences.zh: 子誥，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Gao has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 錢維城，字宗盤，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Qian Weicheng, style name Zongpan, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weicheng, whose style name was Zongpan, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he took first place among the top tier of jinshi and received appointment as a compiler-expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qianlong he took first place among the top tier of jinshi graduates and was appointed a compiler-expositor.

sentences.zh: 功令，初入翰林，分習清、漢文。

translations.literal: By regulation, newly entered Hanlin bachelors were assigned to study either Manchu or Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, newly entered Hanlin bachelors were assigned to study either Manchu or Chinese.

sentences.zh: 維城習清文，散館列三等。

translations.literal: Weicheng studied Manchu; at the Hanlin disbandment examination he was ranked third class.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng studied Manchu and was ranked third class at the Hanlin disbandment examination.

sentences.zh: 上不懌，曰：「維城豈謂清文不足習耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "Does Weicheng mean that Manchu is not worth studying?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said: "Does Weicheng mean that Manchu is not worth studying?"

sentences.zh: 傅恆為之解。

translations.literal: Fuheng interceded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng interceded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 命再試漢文，上謂詩有疵，賦尚通順，仍留修撰。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him tested again in Chinese; the emperor said his poetry had flaws but his fu was still passable, and he was retained as compiler-expositor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him tested again in Chinese, said his poetry had flaws but his fu was still passable, and retained him as compiler-expositor.

sentences.zh: 是歲即遷右中允，命南書房行走。

translations.literal: That same year he was promoted to Right Assistant Master of the Household and ordered to serve in the Southern Library.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was promoted to Right Assistant Master of the Household and ordered to serve in the Southern Library.

sentences.zh: 三遷，再轉為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he was transferred again to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was transferred again to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 疏請申明律例：「事主殺盜賊移屍，有司輒置勿論。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting clarification of statutory provisions: "When a victim kills a thief or robber and moves the corpse, officials often dismiss the case.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting clarification of the statutory provisions: "When a victim kills a thief or robber and moves the corpse, officials often dismiss the case.

sentences.zh: 本律科移屍罪，反至流徒。

translations.literal: The statute itself prescribes punishment for moving a corpse, which can result in exile or penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the statute itself prescribes punishment for moving a corpse, which can result in exile or penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 請凡殺人律得勿論者，雖移屍仍用本律。

translations.literal: I ask that in every case where the statute on killing permits no punishment, moving the corpse should still be governed by that statute.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that wherever the statute on killing permits no punishment, moving the corpse should still be governed by that statute.

sentences.zh: 殺姦之獄，姦夫拒捕，有司輒用鬥殺律定讞。

translations.literal: In adultery cases, when the adulterer resists arrest officials often sentence under the statute on killing in affray.
translations.idiomatic: In adultery cases, when the adulterer resists arrest officials often sentence under the statute on killing in affray.

sentences.zh: 殺姦殺拒捕者，反重於殺不拒捕者。

translations.literal: Thus killing an adulterer who resists arrest is punished more severely than killing one who does not.
translations.idiomatic: Thus killing an adulterer who resists arrest is punished more severely than killing one who does not resist.

sentences.zh: 請用殺拒捕罪人律勿論。」

translations.literal: I ask that the statute permitting no punishment for killing a criminal who resists arrest be applied."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the statute permitting no punishment for killing a criminal who resists arrest be applied instead."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministry for deliberation and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministry for deliberation and adopted.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命偕內閣學士富察善如貴州會湖廣總督吳達善按治威寧州知州劉標虧帑，巡撫良卿、前巡撫方世俊等皆坐譴。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to proceed to Guizhou with Grand Secretary Fuca Shanru, together with Hu-Guang Governor-General Wu Dashan, to investigate Wei'ning Prefect Liu Biao's embezzlement of treasury funds; Governor Liang Qing, former Governor Fang Shijun, and others were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to Guizhou with Grand Secretary Fuca Shanru, together with Hu-Guang Governor-General Wu Dashan, to investigate the embezzlement of treasury funds by Liu Biao, prefect of Wei'ning; Governor Liang Qing, former Governor Fang Shijun, and others were all punished.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，古州苗香要為亂，復命偕吳達善及巡撫宮兆麟督剿。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Xiang Yao of the Miao at Guzhou raised a rebellion; Weicheng was again ordered to join Wu Dashan and Governor Gong Zhaolin in directing suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Xiang Yao of the Miao at Guzhou raised a rebellion, and Weicheng was again ordered to join Wu Dashan and Governor Gong Zhaolin in directing the suppression.

sentences.zh: 香要多力而狡，苗女迫根為羽翼，煽旁寨出掠。

translations.literal: Xiang Yao was powerful and cunning; the Miao woman Po Gen served as his wing, inciting neighboring stockades to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yao was powerful and cunning; the Miao woman Po Gen served as his right hand, inciting neighboring stockades to raid.

sentences.zh: 維城如古州，督總兵程國相破烏牛、佳居諸寨，獲迫根。

translations.literal: Weicheng went to Guzhou and directed Regional Commander Cheng Guoxiang in breaking the stockades at Wuniu, Jiaju, and elsewhere, capturing Po Gen.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng went to Guzhou and directed Regional Commander Cheng Guoxiang in breaking the stockades at Wuniu, Jiaju, and elsewhere, capturing Po Gen.

sentences.zh: 維城乃自烏牛如佳居宣諭，解脅從。

translations.literal: Weicheng then went from Wuniu to Jiaju to proclaim imperial policy and release those who had been coerced into following the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng then went from Wuniu to Jiaju to proclaim imperial policy and release those who had been coerced into following the rebels.

sentences.zh: 督兵破朋論大箐，香要獨身跳去。

translations.literal: He directed troops to break Penglun Daqing; Xiang Yao alone leaped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He directed troops to break Penglun Daqing, but Xiang Yao alone leaped away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 乃令先撤兵，遣诇香要，卒擒而殲之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the troops withdrawn first and sent men to scout out Xiang Yao; in the end he was captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the troops withdrawn first and sent men to scout out Xiang Yao; in the end Xiang Yao was captured and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 亂定，諭議敘。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was settled, an edict ordered rewards to be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was settled, an edict ordered that rewards be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，雲南龍陵戍卒四十去伍走，既就獲，大吏請悉誅之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year forty garrison soldiers at Longling in Yunnan deserted; once recaptured, senior officials requested that all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year forty garrison soldiers at Longling in Yunnan deserted; once they were recaptured, senior officials requested that all be executed.

sentences.zh: 維城入對，言：「伊犁戍卒荷校一月，今用法過重。

translations.literal: Weicheng presented himself for audience and said: "Garrison soldiers at Yili wear the cangue for one month; the punishment now proposed is too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng presented himself for audience and said: "Garrison soldiers at Yili wear the cangue for one month; the punishment now proposed is too severe.

sentences.zh: 且戮於獲所，邊兵何由知？

translations.literal: Moreover, if they are executed where they were captured, how will border troops learn of it?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if they are executed where they were captured, how will border troops learn of it?

sentences.zh: 不如械至龍陵，倍其罰，荷校三月，足以儆眾。」

translations.literal: It would be better to send them in fetters to Longling, double the penalty, and make them wear the cangue for three months — enough to warn the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to send them in fetters to Longling, double the penalty, and make them wear the cangue for three months — enough to warn the multitude."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，丁父憂，歸，以毀卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, upon his father's death he returned home and died from grief in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, upon his father's death he returned home and died from grief in mourning.

sentences.zh: 諡文敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 維城工文翰，畫山水幽深沈厚。

translations.literal: Weicheng was skilled in literary composition; his landscape painting was deep, remote, and richly subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng was skilled in literary composition, and his landscape painting was deep, remote, and richly subdued.

sentences.zh: 錢陳群謂維城通籍後畫益工，蓋得益於邦達雲。

translations.literal: Qian Chenqun said Weicheng's painting grew still more accomplished after entering official service, having benefited from Bangda, no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chenqun said Weicheng's painting grew still more accomplished after entering official service, having no doubt benefited from Bangda.

sentences.zh: 鄒一桂，字原褒，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Zou Yigui, style name Yuanbao, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yigui, whose style name was Yuanbao, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 祖忠倚，順治九年一甲一名進士，官修撰。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhongyi was top jinshi of the first rank in the ninth year of Shunzhi and served as compiler-expositor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhongyi was the top jinshi of the first rank in the ninth year of Shunzhi and served as a compiler-expositor.

sentences.zh: 一桂，雍正五年二甲一名進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Yigui, in the fifth year of Yongzheng, was first among the second tier of jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui, in the fifth year of Yongzheng, was first among the second tier of jinshi graduates, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，授雲南道監察御史，疏禁官媒蓄婦女為奸利。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed censor of the Yunnan circuit and memorialized to prohibit official matchmakers from keeping women for illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed censor of the Yunnan circuit and memorialized to prohibit official matchmakers from keeping women for illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，轉禮科給事中，疏言：「刑部諸囚已結入北監，未結羈南所。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Board of Rites and memorialized: "Prisoners whose cases are closed enter the northern prison; those whose cases are open are detained in the southern holding quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Board of Rites and memorialized: "Prisoners whose cases are closed enter the northern prison, while those whose cases remain open are detained in the southern holding quarters.

sentences.zh: 今察視監所，已未結雜收，請如例分禁。」

translations.literal: On inspection of the prisons, closed and open cases are now mixed together; I ask that they be separated and confined according to regulation."
translations.idiomatic: On inspection of the prisons, closed and open cases are now mixed together; I ask that they be separated and confined according to regulation."

sentences.zh: 又言：「奉命下部議諸事，科道輒於部議未上之先，攙越凟陳，請申飭。」

translations.literal: He also said: "On matters ordered referred to the ministry for deliberation, censors repeatedly submit memorials ahead of the ministry's report, presumptuously and insolently; I ask that this be sternly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "On matters ordered referred to the ministry for deliberation, censors repeatedly submit memorials ahead of the ministry's report, presumptuously and insolently; I ask that this be sternly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫許容坐誣劾糧道謝濟世罷，復命署湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Xu Rong was dismissed for falsely impeaching Grain Intendant Xie Jishi; he was again ordered to serve as acting governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Governor Xu Rong was dismissed for falsely impeaching Grain Intendant Xie Jishi, but was again ordered to serve as acting governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 一桂與給事中陳大玠具疏論列，謂：「容狡詐欺公，僅予奪職，已邀寬典；

translations.literal: Yigui and Supervising Secretary Chen Dajue jointly submitted a detailed memorial, stating: "Rong was cunning and deceptive toward the public; to strip him of office only was already an indulgent measure;
translations.idiomatic: Yigui and Supervising Secretary Chen Dajue jointly submitted a detailed memorial, stating: "Rong was cunning and deceptive toward the public; to strip him of office only was already an indulgent measure;

sentences.zh: 今復任封疆，何以訓天下？

translations.literal: now to restore him to a frontier governorship — how will the empire be instructed?
translations.idiomatic: now to restore him to a frontier governorship — how will the empire be instructed?

sentences.zh: 乞降旨宣示臣民，俾曉然於黜陟之所以然，斯國法昭而吏治有所率循。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to make officials and people clearly understand the principles of promotion and dismissal, so that national law is manifest and official governance has a standard to follow."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict be issued to make officials and people clearly understand the principles of promotion and dismissal, so that national law is manifest and official governance has a standard to follow."

sentences.zh: 上為罷容。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Rong on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Rong on this account.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷太常寺少卿，疏言：「律載獄俱全圖，鐵索鈕钅，俱有定式。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized: "The code provides full diagrams for prisons, iron chains, shackles, and fetters, all with fixed forms.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized: "The code provides full diagrams for prisons, iron chains, shackles, and fetters, all with fixed forms.

sentences.zh: 獄官以防範為辭，匣床以束其身，鐵簫以直其項，觀音圈以攣其手足。

translations.literal: Prison officials use prevention as a pretext: the coffin-bed to bind the body, the iron flute to straighten the neck, the Guanyin ring to twist the hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: Prison officials use prevention as a pretext: the coffin-bed to bind the body, the iron flute to straighten the neck, and the Guanyin ring to twist the hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 部議禁非刑，日久复創新制，令諸囚排頭仰臥，橫穿長木，壓其手足，與匣床無異，請敕嚴禁。」

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and prohibited torture, but in time new devices were invented, forcing prisoners to lie face up in a row with a long pole run horizontally through to pin down hands and feet — no different from the coffin-bed; I ask that an imperial order strictly forbid this."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had deliberated and prohibited torture, but in time new devices were invented, forcing prisoners to lie face up in a row with a long pole run horizontally through to pin down their hands and feet — no different from the coffin-bed; I ask that an imperial order strictly forbid this."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四遷為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 同部侍郎張泰開舉一桂子志伊為國子監學正，又坐徇尚書王安國、左都御史楊錫紱祀其父鄉賢，屢下部議，二十一年，左授內閣學士。

translations.literal: Fellow vice minister Zhang Taikai recommended Yigui's son Zhiyi for the post of director of study at the Directorate of Education; Yigui was also punished for showing favoritism to Minister Wang Anguo and Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Xifu in enshrining their fathers as local worthies — the case was repeatedly referred for deliberation — and in the twenty-first year he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow Vice Minister Zhang Taikai recommended Yigui's son Zhiyi for the post of director of study at the Directorate of Education; Yigui was also punished for showing favoritism toward Minister Wang Anguo and Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Xifu in enshrining their fathers as local worthies. The case was repeatedly referred for deliberation, and in the twenty-first year he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，詣京師祝上壽，加禮部侍郎銜，在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; he was granted the rank of Vice Minister of Rites and allowed to draw salary while remaining in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; he was granted the rank of Vice Minister of Rites and allowed to draw salary while remaining in his native place.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，歸，卒於東昌道中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, on his way home, he died on the road in Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, on his way home, he died on the road in Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 加尚書銜。

translations.literal: The rank of Minister was posthumously granted.
translations.idiomatic: The rank of Minister was posthumously granted.

sentences.zh: 一桂畫工花卉，承惲格後為專家。

translations.literal: Yigui was skilled in flower-and-bird painting and, after Yun Shouping, became a leading specialist.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui was skilled in flower-and-bird painting and, after Yun Shouping, became a leading specialist.

sentences.zh: 嘗作百花卷，花題一詩，進上，上深賞之，為題百絕句。

translations.literal: He once painted a scroll of a hundred flowers, inscribing one poem for each blossom; he presented it to the throne, and the emperor greatly admired it and composed a hundred quatrains in response.
translations.idiomatic: He once painted a scroll of a hundred flowers, inscribing one poem for each blossom; he presented it to the throne, and the emperor greatly admired it and composed a hundred quatrains in response.

sentences.zh: 晚被薄譴，歸猶賦詩餞之雲。

translations.literal: In his later years he received a mild reprimand; even when he returned home the emperor still composed verses to see him off, they say.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he received a mild reprimand; even when he returned home the emperor still composed verses to see him off, they say.

sentences.zh: 謝墉，字昆城，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Xie Yong, style name Kuncheng, was a native of Jiashan, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yong, whose style name was Kuncheng, came from Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，上南巡，墉以優貢生召試，賜舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, when the emperor toured the south, Yong, as an outstanding tribute student, was summoned for examination, granted juren status, and appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, when the emperor toured the south, Yong, as an outstanding tribute student, was summoned for examination, granted juren status, and appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 坐撰閩浙總督喀爾吉善碑文語失當，下部議，降調。

translations.literal: He was punished because language in an epitaph he composed for Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Ka'erjishan was inappropriate; the case was referred to the ministry and he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished because language in an epitaph he composed for Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Ka'erjishan was inappropriate; the case was referred to the ministry and he was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，回部平，墉擬鐃歌上，上命复官，直上書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the western regions were pacified, Yong drafted triumphal hymns and presented them; the emperor ordered his rank restored and had him serve directly in the Upper Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when the western regions were pacified, Yong drafted triumphal hymns and presented them; the emperor ordered his rank restored and had him serve directly in the Upper Library.

sentences.zh: 五遷工部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Vice Minister of Works and served as educational commissioner for Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became Vice Minister of Works and served as educational commissioner for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was transferred to the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was transferred to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廣西全州知州彭曰龍坐縱革役复充，奪官，詣部請捐复。

translations.literal: Peng Yuelong, prefect of Quanzhou in Guangxi, was stripped of office for allowing dismissed corvée laborers to be re-enrolled; he came to the ministry to request reinstatement by purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuelong, prefect of Quanzhou in Guangxi, was stripped of office for allowing dismissed corvée laborers to be re-enrolled; he came to the ministry to request reinstatement by purchase.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂領吏部，將許之，墉以為不可。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Agui, acting head of the Board of Personnel, was about to grant the request, but Yong held that it should not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui, acting head of the Board of Personnel, was about to grant the request, but Yong held that it should not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 時有山東商河教諭侯華捐复，方議駁，墉援以例曰龍。

translations.literal: At the time Shanghe Instructor Hou Hua in Shandong was also seeking reinstatement by purchase and the case was under deliberation for rejection; Yong cited that precedent against Yuelong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shanghe Instructor Hou Hua in Shandong was also seeking reinstatement by purchase and the case was under deliberation for rejection; Yong cited that precedent against Yuelong.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疑墉為華地，奏聞。

translations.literal: Agui suspected Yong was pulling strings for Hua and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Agui suspected Yong was pulling strings for Hua and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命訊，華力言無囑託，乃用墉議，不許曰龍捐复。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Hua insisted there had been no solicitation; Yong's opinion was followed and Yuelong's purchase of reinstatement was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Hua insisted there had been no solicitation; Yong's opinion was followed and Yuelong's purchase of reinstatement was denied.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，复督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he again served as educational commissioner for Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he again served as educational commissioner for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，任滿，還京師。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, when his term ended, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year, when his term ended, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上問洪澤湖運河水勢，墉奏：「洪澤湖漸高，民間傳說'昔如釜，今如盤'，請加疏濬。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the water conditions of Hongze Lake and the Grand Canal; Yong reported: "Hongze Lake is gradually rising; among the people it is said that "in the past it was like a cauldron, now it is like a platter." I ask that dredging be increased."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about the water conditions of Hongze Lake and the Grand Canal; Yong reported: "Hongze Lake is gradually rising; among the people it is said that "in the past it was like a cauldron, now it is like a platter." I ask that dredging be increased."

sentences.zh: 五十二年，上以總督李世傑奏洪澤湖水注清口暢流，命墉往與世傑勘湖水淺深。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year the emperor, on the basis of Governor-General Li Shijie's report that Hongze Lake's waters were flowing freely into the Qing estuary, ordered Yong to go and survey the lake's depth with Shijie.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year the emperor, on the basis of Governor-General Li Shijie's report that Hongze Lake's waters were flowing freely into the Qing estuary, ordered Yong to go and survey the lake's depth with Shijie.

sentences.zh: 尋奏湖水深至十丈，淺亦在一二丈間，墉自請議處。

translations.literal: Soon it was reported that the lake was as deep as ten zhang in places and even in shallows one or two zhang; Yong voluntarily requested disciplinary action.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was reported that the lake was as deep as ten zhang in places and even in the shallows one or two zhang; Yong voluntarily requested disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 上以湖水前年較淺，墉得自傳聞，據以入告，茲既已勘明，免其議處。

translations.literal: The emperor said that the lake had indeed been shallower the year before, that Yong had acted on hearsay in reporting as he did, and that now the facts were verified, so disciplinary action was waived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that the lake had indeed been shallower the year before, that Yong had acted on hearsay in reporting as he did, and that now the facts had been verified, so disciplinary action was waived.

sentences.zh: 墉兩任江蘇學政，士有不得志者，以偶語譏誚。

translations.literal: Yong twice served as Jiangsu education commissioner; scholars who had failed to advance mocked him in casual remarks.
translations.idiomatic: Yong served twice as education commissioner of Jiangsu; discontented scholars mocked him in offhand jibes.

sentences.zh: 阿桂偶以聞，上命巡撫閔鶚元訪察。

translations.literal: Agui happened to hear of it; the emperor ordered Governor Min E'yuan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Agui happened to hear of it, and the emperor ordered the governor Min E'yuan to look into the matter.

sentences.zh: 鶚元言墉初任聲名平常，後任頗為謹飭。

translations.literal: E'yuan said that in Yong's first term his reputation was ordinary, but in his second he was quite disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: E'yuan reported that Yong's first term had been undistinguished, but his second was markedly careful and restrained.

sentences.zh: 上命降授內閣學士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him demoted to Grand Secretariat scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him demoted and appointed Grand Secretariat scholar.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，上察直上書房諸臣多曠班，墉七日未入直，复降編修，在修書處效力。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, noting many absentees among those on duty in the Upper Library, the emperor found Yong had not reported for seven days and again demoted him to compiler, ordering him to serve in the editorial bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year the emperor, finding many of those on duty in the Upper Library absent without leave, saw that Yong had not reported for seven days and again demoted him to compiler, assigning him to serve in the editorial bureau.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，復命直上書房。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was again ordered to serve directly in the Upper Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he was again ordered back to direct service in the Upper Library.

sentences.zh: 六十年，休致。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 墉在上書房久，仁宗方典學，肄習詩文，高宗命墉講授。

translations.literal: Yong had long served in the Upper Library; the Jiaqing Emperor, then heir apparent, was studying the classics and practicing poetry and prose, and the Qianlong Emperor ordered Yong to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had served long in the Upper Library. The future Jiaqing Emperor was then mastering the classics and practicing poetry and prose, and the Qianlong Emperor ordered Yong to teach him.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，加恩舊學，贈三品卿銜，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, in reward for his old service as tutor, he was posthumously granted third-rank ministerial title and imperial rites of mourning and burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, in gratitude for his old service as tutor, he was posthumously granted third-rank ministerial title and the imperial rites of mourning and burial.

sentences.zh: 子恭銘，進士，改庶吉士，散館歸班，是歲授內閣中書。

translations.literal: His son Gongming was a jinshi, became a Hanlin bachelor, and after completing the probationary period returned to the regular roster; that year he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongming was a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the probationary academy returned to the regular roster; that same year he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 墉以督學蒙謗，然江南稱其得士，尤賞江都汪中，嘗字之曰：「予上容甫，爵也；

translations.literal: Though Yong was slandered as education commissioner, Jiangnan praised him for recognizing talent, especially Wang Zhong of Jiangdu; he once addressed him by style name, saying: "If I stand above Rongfu, that is by rank;
translations.idiomatic: Though Yong was maligned for his work as education commissioner, Jiangnan praised him for finding true talent, above all Wang Zhong of Jiangdu. He once addressed him by style name, saying: "If I stand above Rongfu, that is rank alone;

sentences.zh: 若以學，予於容甫北面矣！」

translations.literal: but if learning is the measure, I should face north toward Rongfu!"
translations.idiomatic: but if learning is the measure, I should face north and bow to Rongfu!"

sentences.zh: 乾隆中直上書房諸臣以學行稱者，又有金甡、莊存與、劉星煒。

translations.literal: Among those in the Upper Library during the Qianlong reign who were renowned for learning and conduct were also Jin Shen, Zhuang Cunyu, and Liu Xingwei.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who served in the Upper Library under Qianlong and were famed for learning and conduct were also Jin Shen, Zhuang Cunyu, and Liu Xingwei.

sentences.zh: 甡，字雨叔，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Shen, style name Yushu, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, whose style name was Yushu, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初以舉人授國子監學正。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate, he was appointed academician of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a provincial graduate appointed academician of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，舉禮部試第一，廷試复第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination and again first in the palace examination, and was appointed a drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong he placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination and again first in the palace examination, and was appointed a drafter.

sentences.zh: 三遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three promotions to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，直上書房，擢詹事，再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he entered the Upper Library directly, was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent, and then again to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was posted directly to the Upper Library, promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent, and then again to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上幸熱河，從，方入直，遘疾遽僕。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the emperor went to Rehe, he accompanied him; just as he was entering duty he was stricken with illness and suddenly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, when the emperor traveled to Rehe, he went along; just as he was entering duty he was seized by illness and suddenly fell.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉統勳以聞，命予假。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun reported this, and the emperor granted him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun reported it, and the emperor granted him leave.

sentences.zh: 甡乞休，允之。

translations.literal: Shen requested retirement and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shen begged to retire, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，疾間，乃得歸。

translations.literal: The following autumn, when his illness had abated, he was able to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn, when his illness had eased, he was at last able to go home.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he died, at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 甡在上書房十七年，直諒誠敬，所陳說必正義法言，諸皇子皇孫皆愛重之。

translations.literal: Shen served seventeen years in the Upper Library; upright, candid, and sincere in respect, whatever he expounded was righteous discourse within the bounds of propriety, and all the imperial sons and grandsons held him in affection and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Shen spent seventeen years in the Upper Library. Upright, candid, and reverent, he spoke only what was just and within the bounds of propriety, and every prince and imperial grandson held him in affection and esteem.

sentences.zh: 存與，字方耕，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Cunyu, style name Fanggen, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cunyu, whose style name was Fanggen, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he was a jinshi of the second rank in the first tier and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qianlong he graduated jinshi as second in the first tier and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 四遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He rose through four promotions to Grand Secretariat scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted four times to Grand Secretariat scholar.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，督直隸學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was made education commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed education commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 按試滿洲、蒙古童生，嚴，不得傳遞，群閧。

translations.literal: When he examined Manchu and Mongol boys, he was strict and would not allow messages to be passed; the crowd raised an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When he examined Manchu and Mongol boys he was strict and forbade the passing of notes; the crowd broke into an uproar.

sentences.zh: 御史湯世昌論劾，命奪存與官。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Shichang memorialized in impeachment, and the emperor ordered Cunyu stripped of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Shichang memorialized in impeachment, and the emperor ordered Cunyu deprived of his rank.

sentences.zh: 上惡滿洲、蒙古童生縱恣，親覆試，搜得懷挾文字。

translations.literal: The emperor, disgusted by the unrestrained conduct of Manchu and Mongol boys, personally conducted a re-examination and discovered hidden crib notes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered by the license of Manchu and Mongol boys, personally held a re-examination and uncovered concealed crib sheets.

sentences.zh: 臨鞫，童生海成最狡黠，言：「何不殺之？」

translations.literal: At the interrogation, the boy Haicheng was the most cunning and said: "Why not just kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: At the hearing, the boy Haicheng was the most brazen and said: "Why not just kill him?"

sentences.zh: 上怒，立命誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and immediately ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and at once ordered him put to death.

sentences.zh: 閧堂附和者三人，發拉林種地；

translations.literal: Three who had joined the uproar in the hall were sent to Lalin to work the land;
translations.idiomatic: Three who had joined the hall in the uproar were sent to Lalin to farm;

sentences.zh: 四十人令在旗披甲；

translations.literal: forty were ordered to serve in the banners as soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: forty were ordered to serve in the banners under arms;

sentences.zh: 不得更赴試。

translations.literal: and they were forbidden to take the examinations again.
translations.idiomatic: and none of them might sit for the examinations again.

sentences.zh: 並以存與督試嚴密，仍命留任。

translations.literal: Cunyu was also deemed to have supervised the examination with proper rigor, and he was ordered to remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also judged that Cunyu had supervised the examination with proper rigor, and ordered him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪。

translations.literal: His father died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，補內閣學士，仍授原官，直上書房。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was restored as Grand Secretariat scholar, reassumed his former rank, and returned to the Upper Library.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was restored as Grand Secretariat scholar, reassumed his former rank, and returned to the Upper Library.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪。

translations.literal: His mother died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，補原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，以衰老休致。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he retired on account of age and infirmity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he retired on grounds of age and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he died.

sentences.zh: 存與廉鯁。

translations.literal: Cunyu was upright and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Cunyu was incorruptible and unbending.

sentences.zh: 典浙江試，巡撫餽金不受，遺以二品冠，受之。

translations.literal: When he presided over the Zhejiang examinations the governor sent him gold, which he refused, but left with him a second-rank official's cap, which he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When he presided over the Zhejiang examinations the governor offered him gold, which he refused, but left with him a second-rank official's cap, which he accepted.

sentences.zh: 及塗，從者以告曰：「冠頂真珊瑚，直千金！」

translations.literal: On the road his attendants told him: "The cap finial is genuine coral, worth a thousand in gold!"
translations.idiomatic: On the road his attendants told him: "The cap finial is genuine coral, worth a thousand taels of gold!"

sentences.zh: 存與使千餘裡返之。

translations.literal: Cunyu sent it back more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Cunyu sent it back more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 為講官，上御文華殿，進講禮畢，存與奏：「講章有舛誤，臣意不謂爾。」

translations.literal: As lecturing official, when the emperor took the Hall of Literary Brilliance and the lecture on Rituals was finished, Cunyu memorialized: "There are errors in the lecture text; in my view it should not be so."
translations.idiomatic: As lecturing official, when the emperor attended the Hall of Literary Brilliance and the lecture on Rituals was finished, Cunyu memorialized: "There are errors in the lecture text; in my judgment it should not stand as written."

sentences.zh: 奉書進，复講，盡其旨，上為留聽之。

translations.literal: He presented the book, lectured again, and expounded it fully; the emperor stayed to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the text, lectured again, and expounded it to the full; the emperor remained to listen.

sentences.zh: 弟培因，字本淳，乾隆十五年一甲一名進士，官至內閣學士。

translations.literal: His younger brother Peiyin, style name Benchun, was first among jinshi of the first tier in the fifteenth year of Qianlong and rose to Grand Secretariat scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Peiyin, whose style name was Benchun, was first among jinshi of the first tier in the fifteenth year of Qianlong and rose to Grand Secretariat scholar.

sentences.zh: 劉星煒，字映榆，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Liu Xingwei, style name Yingyu, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingwei, whose style name was Yingyu, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷侍講，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant expositor and made education commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant expositor and appointed education commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「鶴山立縣初，有廣州民一百五戶請修城入籍，緣是開冒考之弊，請以有廬墓、田糧在縣者為限。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When Heshan county was first established, one hundred and fifty Guangzhou households petitioned to register by building walls; this gave rise to the abuse of false registration for examinations. I ask that the limit be set at those who have ancestral halls or tombs and land tax obligations in the county."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When Heshan county was first established, one hundred and fifty Guangzhou households petitioned to register by building walls, and from this arose the abuse of false registration for the examinations. I ask that eligibility be limited to those who have ancestral halls or tombs and land tax obligations within the county."

sentences.zh: 丁母喪，去。

translations.literal: His mother died and he left office.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died and he left his post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 督安徽學政，請童生兼試五言六韻詩。

translations.literal: As education commissioner of Anhui, he requested that boys in the preliminary examination also be tested on regulated verse of five characters in six rhymes.
translations.idiomatic: As education commissioner of Anhui he requested that boys in the preliminary examination also be tested on five-character regulated verse in six rhymes.

sentences.zh: 童試有詩自此始。

translations.literal: From this point poetry appeared in the boys' examinations.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward poetry was included in the boys' examinations.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to attendant reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，直上書房，再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he entered the Upper Library directly and was again promoted to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was posted directly to the Upper Library and again promoted to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 王昶，字德甫，江蘇青浦人。

translations.literal: Wang Chang, style name Defu, was a native of Qingpu, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang, whose style name was Defu, came from Qingpu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the nineteenth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the nineteenth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 南巡，召試，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: During the southern tour he was summoned for examination, appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour he was summoned for examination, appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 三遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to director in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three promotions to director in the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，察治兩淮運鹽提引，前鹽運使盧見曾坐得罪，昶嘗客授見曾所，至是坐漏言奪職。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, while investigating the salt transport surcharge at Lianghuai, former Salt Transport Commissioner Lu Jianzeng was found guilty; Chang had once taught as a guest in Lu's household, and at this time was stripped of his office for leaking information.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, while investigating the salt transport surcharge at Lianghuai, former Salt Transport Commissioner Lu Jianzeng was found guilty. Chang had once taught as a guest in Lu's household, and now was stripped of office for leaking information.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督阿桂帥師討緬甸，疏請發軍前自效。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Agui led troops against Burma; Chang memorialized asking to serve at the front.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Agui led an army against Burma, and Chang memorialized asking to serve at the front.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士傅恆出視師，嗣以理籓院尚書溫福代阿桂，皆以昶佐幕府。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Fu Heng to inspect the army; afterward Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs Wen Fu replaced Agui, and Chang assisted both staffs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Fu Heng to take command in the field; afterward Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs Wen Fu replaced Agui, and Chang served on both staffs.

sentences.zh: 溫福移師討金川，昶實從，疏請敘昶勞，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: When Wen Fu moved his army against Jinchuan, Chang actually followed; a memorial requested recognition of his service and he was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Fu moved his army against Jinchuan, Chang went with him; a memorial requested recognition of his service, and he was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 既，復從阿桂定兩金川，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Afterward he again followed Agui in pacifying the Two Jinchuans and was again promoted to director.
