translations.idiomatic: Afterward he again followed Agui in pacifying the Two Jinchuans and was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎袁守侗按事四川，上命察軍中事，還奏言昶治軍書有勞。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Yuan Shoutong was investigating affairs in Sichuan; the emperor ordered him to inspect military matters, and on return he reported that Chang had rendered distinguished service in managing military documents.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Punishments Yuan Shoutong was investigating affairs in Sichuan; the emperor ordered him to inspect military matters, and on his return he reported that Chang had rendered distinguished service in managing military documents.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，師凱還，擢昶鴻臚寺卿，仍充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when the victorious army returned, Chang was promoted to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and continued to serve as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, when the victorious army returned, Chang was promoted to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and continued as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 三遷左副都御史，外授江西按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to vice censor-in-chief of the Left, then appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three promotions to vice censor-in-chief of the Left, then was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 數月，以憂歸。

translations.literal: Within a few months he returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he returned home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起直隸按察使，未上，移陝西按察使。

translations.literal: He was recalled as surveillance commissioner of Zhili; before taking up the post he was transferred to Shaanxi as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as surveillance commissioner of Zhili; before he could take up the post he was transferred to Shaanxi as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 在陝西凡十年，值回田五為亂，軍興，昶繕守具，佐治軍需，疏請清釐保甲，禁民間蓄軍器。

translations.literal: He served in Shaanxi for ten years altogether. When the Muslim rebel Tian Wu rose in rebellion and warfare began, Chang prepared defenses and supplies, assisted in managing military provisions, and memorialized requesting the reorganization of the baojia system and a ban on civilians hoarding weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Shaanxi for ten years in all. When the Muslim rebel Tian Wu rose in rebellion and war broke out, Chang prepared defenses and supplies, assisted in managing military provisions, and memorialized requesting the reorganization of the baojia system and a ban on civilians keeping weapons.

sentences.zh: 遷雲南布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 河南伊陽民戕知縣，竄匿陝西境未獲，昶如商州督捕，上命俟得賊詣京師覲見。

translations.literal: When a man from Yiyang in Henan killed a magistrate and fled into Shaanxi still at large, Chang went to Shangzhou to oversee the hunt; the emperor ordered that once the culprit was taken he should proceed to the capital for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When a man from Yiyang in Henan killed a magistrate and fled into Shaanxi still at large, Chang went to Shangzhou to oversee the pursuit; the emperor ordered that once the culprit was taken he should come to the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 昶既得賊，入謁上，自陳疲憊，乞改京職，上溫旨慰遣，乃上官。

translations.literal: Once Chang had the culprit, he went to audience, declared himself worn out, and begged for a post in the capital; the emperor sent comforting edicts and he then took up his new office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang had the culprit he went to audience, declared himself worn out, and begged for a post in the capital; the emperor sent warm edicts of reassurance, and he then took up his new office.

sentences.zh: 以雲南銅政事重，撰銅政全書，求調劑補救之法。

translations.literal: Because Yunnan copper administration was a weighty matter, he compiled a comprehensive book on copper policy and sought remedies and adjustments.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yunnan copper administration was a weighty matter, he compiled a comprehensive book on copper policy and sought ways to remedy and adjust it.

sentences.zh: 旋調江西布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，內遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was transferred within the capital to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was transferred within the capital to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 屢命如江南、湖北讞獄。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered to review legal cases in Jiangnan and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to review legal cases in Jiangnan and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，以老乞罷，上許之，方歲暮，諭俟來歲春融歸里。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he begged leave on account of age; the emperor granted it, and as it was year's end, directed him to wait until the spring thaw to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he begged leave on account of age; the emperor granted it, and as the year was ending, directed him to wait until the spring thaw before returning home.

sentences.zh: 昶歸，遂以「春融」名其堂。

translations.literal: When Chang returned, he named his hall "Spring Thaw."
translations.idiomatic: When Chang returned home he named his hall "Spring Thaw."

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，詣京師賀內禪，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he went to the capital to congratulate the abdication and attended the banquet of a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he went to the capital to congratulate the abdication and took part in the banquet of a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 四年，复詣京師謁高宗梓宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again went to the capital to pay respects at the Qianlong Emperor's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again went to the capital to pay respects before the Qianlong Emperor's coffin.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 昶工詩古文辭，通經。

translations.literal: Chang was skilled at classical poetry and prose and thoroughly versed in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was accomplished in classical poetry and prose and thoroughly versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 讀硃子書，兼及薛瑄、王守仁諸家之學。

translations.literal: He read Zhu Xi's works and also studied the teachings of Xue Xuan, Wang Shouren, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He read Zhu Xi's works and also took up the teachings of Xue Xuan, Wang Shouren, and others.

sentences.zh: 蒐採金石，平選詩文詞，著述傳於世。

translations.literal: He collected inscriptions on bronze and stone, compiled and selected poetry and prose, and his writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered inscriptions on bronze and stone, compiled and selected poetry and prose, and his writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國家全盛日，文學侍從之臣，雍容揄揚，潤色鴻業。

translations.literal: Commentary: The historiographer says: In the days of the state's full flourishing, literary attendants carried themselves with easy grace, offering praise and adding luster to the grand enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The historiographer says: In the days of the state's full flourishing, literary attendants moved with easy grace, offering praise and adding luster to the grand enterprise.

sentences.zh: 人主以其閒暇，偶與賡和，一時稱盛事。

translations.literal: The sovereign, in moments of leisure, would occasionally exchange verses with them; for a time it was called a great occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign, in moments of leisure, would occasionally exchange verses with them, and for a time it was hailed as a great occasion.

sentences.zh: 未有彌歲經時，往復酬答，君臣若師友，如高宗之於陳群、德潛。

translations.literal: Never before had exchanges lasted whole years, back and forth in reply, ruler and subject like teacher and friend—as with the Qianlong Emperor and Chen Qun and Deqian.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had exchanges lasted whole years, back and forth in reply, ruler and subject like teacher and friend—as with the Qianlong Emperor toward Chen Qun and Deqian.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，懿矣！

translations.literal: Alas, how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how splendid!

sentences.zh: 當時以儒臣被知遇，或以文辭，或以書畫，錄其尤著者。

translations.literal: At that time Confucian officials who received imperial favor—whether for literary composition or for painting and calligraphy—are recorded here, the most eminent among them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Confucian officials who won imperial favor—whether for literary composition or for painting and calligraphy—are recorded here, the most eminent among them.

sentences.zh: 視陳群、德潛恩禮雖未逮，文采要足與相映，不其盛歟！

translations.literal: Though their grace and favor did not reach the level of Chen Qun and Deqian, their literary brilliance was certainly enough to shine in reciprocal light—is this not grandeur indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Though the grace and favor shown them did not match that given Chen Qun and Deqian, their literary brilliance was certainly enough to shine in answer—is this not grandeur indeed!
